audits.guide.purpose: Plan, launch and track every internal-audit engagement from one register.
audits.guide.description: This is the operational home for audits — create engagements from the annual plan, run fieldwork, and follow each audit through its lifecycle to reporting.
audits.guide.action.filter: Filter by status or audit type, and search by name
audits.guide.action.open: Open an audit to run fieldwork and manage its checklist
audits.guide.action.track: Track progress and status across all engagements
audits.guide.section.create.title: Create an audit
audits.guide.section.create.body: Start a new engagement here — pick a template to preload its checklist. Needs the Create audit permission.
audits.guide.section.filters.title: Filter & search
audits.guide.section.filters.body: Narrow the list by status or audit type. Filters re-query the server, so large registers stay fast.
audits.guide.section.table.title: The audit register
audits.guide.section.table.body: Every engagement with its type, status and progress. Click a row to open it and run fieldwork.
audits.guide.rule.lifecycle: An audit moves Draft → Planned → In progress → Under review → Completed; some transitions are one-way.
audits.guide.rule.template: The checklist is fixed from the chosen template version when the audit starts.
audits.guide.rule.team: Only assigned team members (or a manager) can respond to checklist items.
audits.guide.rule.cancel: A cancelled audit keeps its record and needs a reason — it is never hard-deleted.
audits.guide.tip.filter: Filter before exporting or reviewing to focus on what matters.
audits.guide.tip.template: Preload a checklist by choosing a published template when creating the audit.
audits.guide.tip.reopen: A completed audit can be reopened with a reason if new work is needed.
audits.guide.faq.create.q: Why can't I create an audit?
audits.guide.faq.create.a: Creating an audit needs the Create audit permission (Audit Manager / Administrator).
audits.guide.faq.status.a: They track the lifecycle from Draft through In progress to Completed; the badge colour reflects the current stage.

exceptions.guide.purpose: Raise, track and close audit findings (exceptions) through their management-action-plan lifecycle in one register.
exceptions.guide.description: The findings register for the whole audit function — every exception raised during fieldwork, tracked from open through its MAP (management action plan) approval and remediation to closure.
exceptions.guide.action.filter: Filter findings by status, severity, audit, plan, overdue or recurrence, and search by title.
exceptions.guide.action.open: Open a finding to review it, submit or approve its MAP, and progress it to closure.

exceptions.guide.section.export.body: Download the current filtered findings as a CSV — a shareable snapshot of the register for reporting or offline review.

exceptions.guide.section.table.body: Every finding with its severity, status, owner and target date. Overdue and recurrence flags surface here; click a row to open it.
exceptions.guide.rule.lifecycle: A finding moves Open → MAP submitted → MAP approved → Pending closure → Closed; a rejected MAP returns it for rework.
exceptions.guide.rule.map: A management action plan must be submitted and approved before a finding can progress to closure.
exceptions.guide.rule.overdue: A finding is flagged overdue once past its target date, with the days-past count shown.
exceptions.guide.rule.recurrence: A finding marked as a recurrence repeats an issue from a prior audit and is highlighted for escalation.
exceptions.guide.tip.filter: Filter to open or overdue findings before exporting to focus follow-up.
exceptions.guide.tip.overdue: Use the overdue filter to drive remediation chasing and status meetings.
exceptions.guide.tip.export: Export a filtered CSV for audit-committee packs or offline review.
exceptions.guide.faq.map.a: A management action plan — the owner's committed remediation, which an audit manager approves before the finding can close.
exceptions.guide.faq.overdue.q: Why is a finding flagged overdue?
exceptions.guide.faq.overdue.a: Its target remediation date has passed without closure; the register shows how many days it is past due.

risk.guide.description: The central home for operational and enterprise risks: register each risk, rate it by likelihood × impact, assign an owner and treatment, and follow it from open to closed.

risk.guide.action.score: Open a risk to edit and re-score its likelihood × impact

risk.guide.section.register.body: Add a new risk here, then set its likelihood, impact, owner and treatment. Needs the Manage risk permission.
risk.guide.section.filters.title: Filter & search
risk.guide.section.filters.body: Narrow the register by status or severity band, or search by title; filters re-query the server so large registers stay fast.
risk.guide.section.table.title: The risk register
risk.guide.section.table.body: Every risk with its category, owner, likelihood × impact rating, status and target date. Use the row menu to edit or change status.
risk.guide.rule.rating: The severity band (low → critical) is derived from likelihood × impact.
risk.guide.rule.lifecycle: A risk moves Open → Assessed → Mitigating → Monitoring → Closed.
risk.guide.rule.owner: Every risk needs an owner accountable for its treatment.
risk.guide.rule.close: Closing a risk requires a rationale and is captured in its history.
risk.guide.tip.residual: Record the residual likelihood × impact after treatment to show the risk reduction.
risk.guide.tip.heatmap: Open the heatmap to see the whole register plotted by likelihood and impact.
risk.guide.tip.closed: Tick 'Include closed' to review historic risks alongside active ones.
risk.guide.faq.rating.q: How is the severity band calculated?
risk.guide.faq.rating.a: It comes from likelihood × impact — the higher the product, the higher the band (low → critical).
risk.guide.faq.close.q: Should I delete a risk or close it?
risk.guide.faq.close.a: Prefer closing with a rationale to keep an audit trail; deletion is permanent and needs the Manage risk permission.
controls.guide.purpose: Maintain the register of internal controls — their type, testing frequency and effectiveness.
controls.guide.description: This is the system of record for internal controls: register each control, classify how it works, record effectiveness testing, and link it to the risks and regulations it addresses.
controls.guide.action.filter: Filter by type or effectiveness, and search by code or title
controls.guide.action.test: Edit a control to record its effectiveness testing result

controls.guide.section.filters.title: Filter & search
controls.guide.section.filters.body: Narrow the register by control type or effectiveness, toggle retired controls, or search by code or title.
controls.guide.section.table.title: The controls register
controls.guide.section.table.body: Every control with its owner, type, frequency, tested effectiveness and status. Use the row menu to edit, retire or delete.
controls.guide.rule.testing: Recording an effectiveness result requires a last-tested date; setting it to Not tested clears that date.
controls.guide.rule.retire: Retiring a control keeps its history — it stays in the register and is never hard-deleted by default.
controls.guide.rule.code: Each control carries a unique code used to reference it from findings and reports.
controls.guide.rule.type: A control is classified as preventive, detective, corrective or directive.
controls.guide.tip.filter: Filter by effectiveness to surface ineffective or untested controls that need attention.
controls.guide.tip.retire: Retire a control instead of deleting it to preserve its testing and finding history.
controls.guide.tip.compliance: Open the Controls compliance analytics from the header to see coverage and effectiveness trends.
controls.guide.faq.register.q: Why can't I register or edit a control?
controls.guide.faq.register.a: Registering, editing and retiring controls needs the Manage controls permission; without it the register is read-only.
controls.guide.faq.effectiveness.q: What do the effectiveness values mean?
controls.guide.faq.effectiveness.a: They record the result of effectiveness testing — Not tested, Effective, Partially effective or Ineffective — with a last-tested date required once a control is tested.

universe.guide.rule.residual: The composite residual score is derived from the entity's weighted risk-dimension scores.
universe.guide.rule.heat: Heat bands map the residual score onto low / moderate / high / critical for at-a-glance ranking.
universe.guide.rule.archive: Entities are archived rather than deleted, so history and past audits are preserved.
universe.guide.rule.score: Updating risk scores needs the Score risk permission; managing entities needs Manage universe.
universe.guide.tip.import: Use Bulk import to load a large universe at once instead of adding entities one by one.

universe.guide.tip.archived: Tick Include archived to review entities that were retired from the active universe.
universe.guide.faq.residual.q: How is the composite residual score calculated?
universe.guide.faq.residual.a: It aggregates the entity's scores across the configured risk dimensions into a single residual value, which drives its heat band.
universe.guide.faq.delete.a: No — entities are archived instead of deleted so their audit history is kept; archived entities can be shown with the Include archived filter.

planning.guide.tip.revisions: Use request revisions to send a plan back with feedback instead of rejecting it outright.
planning.guide.faq.create.q: Why can't I create a plan?
planning.guide.faq.create.a: Creating and editing plans needs the Manage plan permission, held by Audit Managers.
planning.guide.faq.audits.q: How do plans turn into audits?
planning.guide.faq.audits.a: Once a plan is approved, its plan items are used to launch the audit engagements for that period.
identity.guide.purpose: Browse and manage every user in the identity directory from one place.
identity.guide.description: The identity directory lists all users provisioned from Active Directory, showing each one's roles, status and last login so administrators can keep access accurate and current.
identity.guide.action.search: Search users by name or email
identity.guide.action.filter: Filter the directory by role or account status
identity.guide.action.open: Open a user to review their profile, roles and activity
identity.guide.action.deactivate: Deactivate a user to revoke their access
identity.guide.section.filters.title: Filter & search
identity.guide.section.filters.body: Narrow the directory by role or status, or search by name or email; filters re-query the server so large directories stay fast.
identity.guide.section.table.title: The user directory
identity.guide.section.table.body: Every user with their email, status and last login; click a row to open the profile, or use the row menu to view details or deactivate.
identity.guide.rule.provisioned: Users are provisioned from Active Directory — accounts are not created manually here.
identity.guide.rule.awaiting: A new user stays in Awaiting role assignment until an administrator grants a role.
identity.guide.rule.deactivate: Deactivating a user revokes access but keeps the record; deactivated users are never hard-deleted.
identity.guide.tip.search: Combine search with a role or status filter to pinpoint a user quickly.
identity.guide.tip.awaiting: Filter by Awaiting role assignment to find newly provisioned users who still need access.
identity.guide.faq.create.q: Why can't I add a new user here?
identity.guide.faq.create.a: Users are provisioned automatically from Active Directory; you assign roles and manage status here rather than creating accounts.
identity.guide.faq.status.q: What do the account statuses mean?
identity.guide.faq.status.a: Active can sign in, Awaiting role assignment has no role yet, Deactivated has had access revoked, and Locked is temporarily blocked.
dashboard.guide.title: Dashboard
dashboard.guide.purpose: Your personalised control centre — a read-only overview of audit health, open findings and quick access to every module.
dashboard.guide.description: The home dashboard aggregates live data from across AuditX — KPI cards, analytics charts and an attention list of open critical and high findings — then launches you into the module you need.
dashboard.guide.action.kpis: Review headline KPIs — audits in flight, plan execution, and open and closed findings
dashboard.guide.action.charts: Explore analytics charts for audit status and findings by severity, age and root cause
dashboard.guide.action.attention: Triage open critical and high findings from the attention list
dashboard.guide.action.launch: Jump straight into any module from the quick-launch grid
dashboard.guide.section.kpis.title: KPI cards
dashboard.guide.section.kpis.body: At-a-glance metrics that adapt to your permissions; click a card to open its module. Without analytics access you get a governance summary instead.
dashboard.guide.section.charts.title: Analytics charts
dashboard.guide.section.charts.body: Live breakdowns of audit status and of findings by severity, age and root cause — needs the View analytics permission.
dashboard.guide.section.attention.title: Needs attention
dashboard.guide.section.attention.body: Open critical and high findings within the chosen window. Use the toggles to filter, then click a row to open the finding.
dashboard.guide.section.launch.title: Quick access
dashboard.guide.section.launch.body: Shortcut tiles to every workspace you can open — only the modules your role permits appear here.
dashboard.guide.rule.readonly: The dashboard is read-only — you review and navigate here, but make changes inside each module.
dashboard.guide.rule.permission: Cards and charts adapt to your permissions; without View analytics you see a governance summary rather than audit metrics.
dashboard.guide.rule.attention: The attention list shows only open Critical and High findings raised within the selected look-back window.
dashboard.guide.rule.launch: Quick-launch tiles are filtered to the modules your role can access.
dashboard.guide.tip.filter: Use the severity and period toggles to focus the attention list on what matters now.
dashboard.guide.tip.kpi: Click any KPI card to jump straight to the module behind it.
dashboard.guide.tip.analytics: Ask an administrator for the View analytics permission to unlock the charts and finding metrics.
dashboard.guide.faq.charts.q: Why don't I see any charts?
dashboard.guide.faq.charts.a: The analytics charts need the View analytics permission; without it the dashboard shows a session-based governance summary instead.
dashboard.guide.faq.attention.q: What is in the Needs attention list?
dashboard.guide.faq.attention.a: Open Critical and High findings from the selected period — click a row to open the finding in the Exceptions module.
templatesAdmin.guide.purpose: Create and manage the versioned audit checklist templates your organization uses to preload new audits.
templatesAdmin.guide.description: This admin console lists every checklist template with its audit type, publish status, current version, and item count. Templates move from draft to published, and published ones are used to preload the checklist when an audit is launched, giving every engagement a consistent, organization-configured starting point.
templatesAdmin.guide.action.create: Create a new draft checklist template for a given audit type.
templatesAdmin.guide.action.filter: Filter templates by search text, audit type, or status.
templatesAdmin.guide.action.clone: Clone an existing template as the starting point for a new one.
templatesAdmin.guide.action.archive: Archive a template to retire it, or restore an archived one.
templatesAdmin.guide.section.create.body: Start a new draft template; you then add checklist items and publish it when ready. Requires the Manage Templates permission.
templatesAdmin.guide.section.filters.bod: Narrow the list by name search, audit type, or status (draft, published, archived) to find the template you need.
templatesAdmin.guide.section.table.title: Templates table
templatesAdmin.guide.section.table.body: Each row shows the template name, audit type, status, current version, and item count. Click a row to open it, or use the row menu to clone or archive.
templatesAdmin.guide.flow.draft: Create a draft template and pick its audit type.
templatesAdmin.guide.flow.items: Add and order the checklist items and their guidance.
templatesAdmin.guide.flow.publish: Publish the draft so it becomes available to audits.
templatesAdmin.guide.flow.preload: Launching an audit preloads its checklist from the published template.
templatesAdmin.guide.flow.revise: Clone or draft a new version to revise without disrupting live audits.
templatesAdmin.guide.dep.auditType: Audit-type reference data, which classifies each template.
templatesAdmin.guide.dep.permissions: The Manage Templates permission, required to create, clone, or archive.
templatesAdmin.guide.dep.bank: Your organization's configuration, since templates are organization-specific.
templatesAdmin.guide.use.audits: Audits, which preload their checklist from a published template.
templatesAdmin.guide.use.checklist: The audit checklist executed by auditors during fieldwork.
templatesAdmin.guide.use.findings: Findings and exceptions raised against checklist items during an audit.
templatesAdmin.guide.rule.versioning: Templates are versioned; the list shows the current version number.
templatesAdmin.guide.rule.publish: Only published templates can be used to preload an audit checklist.
templatesAdmin.guide.rule.archive: Archiving retires a template from selection without deleting its history; it can be restored.
templatesAdmin.guide.rule.clone: Cloning copies a template's items into a fresh draft, leaving the source untouched.
templatesAdmin.guide.tip.clone: Clone a proven template instead of building a similar one from scratch.
templatesAdmin.guide.tip.status: Use the status filter to separate live published templates from work-in-progress drafts.
templatesAdmin.guide.tip.auditType: Tag each template with the correct audit type so it surfaces when the matching audit is launched.
templatesAdmin.guide.perm.manage: Users with Manage Templates can create, clone, publish, and archive templates.
templatesAdmin.guide.perm.view: Other authorised users can view and open templates but not change them.
templatesAdmin.guide.faq.publish.q: How does a template become usable by audits?
templatesAdmin.guide.faq.publish.a: Add its checklist items while it is a draft, then publish it; published templates are offered when launching a matching audit.
templatesAdmin.guide.faq.edit.q: Can I change a template that audits already use?
templatesAdmin.guide.faq.edit.a: Templates are versioned, so revise via a new version or a clone; existing audits keep the checklist version they were preloaded with.
sanctions.guide.purpose: Track disciplinary sanction cases that arise from audit findings, from HR recommendation through to disciplinary-committee decision and appeal.
sanctions.guide.description: The sanctions tracker is the register of disciplinary cases opened when audit findings point to individual misconduct. Each case follows a governed lifecycle — recommendation to HR, HR outcome, disciplinary-committee (DC) referral and decision, then optional appeal — while the subject employee's identity stays masked to protect privacy. Use it to monitor where every case sits and to ensure consistent, auditable follow-through.
sanctions.guide.action.filter: Filter cases by lifecycle status to focus on those awaiting action.
sanctions.guide.action.open: Open a case row to view its full disciplinary history and record the next step.
sanctions.guide.action.track: Track severity, category and recurrence to spot repeat offenders and high-risk cases.
sanctions.guide.section.filters.title: Status filter
sanctions.guide.section.filters.body: Narrow the register to a single lifecycle stage — such as awaiting HR outcome, referred to the disciplinary committee, or under appeal — to prioritise pending work.
sanctions.guide.section.table.title: Case register
sanctions.guide.section.table.body: Each row is one disciplinary case showing severity, current status, category, recurrence and the date it was triggered; click a row to open the full case.
sanctions.guide.section.masked.title: Masked subject
sanctions.guide.section.masked.body: The subject employee is shown as EMPLOYEE_REDACTED unless you hold clearance to view identities, keeping disciplinary matters confidential.
sanctions.guide.flow.finding: An audit finding identifies individual misconduct or a control breach.
sanctions.guide.flow.recommendation: A sanction recommendation is drafted and submitted to HR.
sanctions.guide.flow.hr: HR records the disciplinary outcome for the subject.
sanctions.guide.flow.dc: The case is referred to the disciplinary committee, which records its decision.
sanctions.guide.flow.appeal: The subject may appeal, and the appeal decision is recorded to close the case.
sanctions.guide.dep.findings: Findings — sanction cases originate from findings raised during an audit.
sanctions.guide.dep.audits: Audits — the engagement that produced the finding provides the case context.
sanctions.guide.dep.identity: Identity — user directory resolves and masks the subject employee's name.
sanctions.guide.use.reports: Reports — sanction outcomes feed disciplinary and HR compliance reporting.
sanctions.guide.use.analytics: Analytics — case volumes, severities and recurrence surface in dashboards.
sanctions.guide.use.notifications: Notifications — status changes alert HR and disciplinary-committee owners.
sanctions.guide.rule.masking: Subject identities are masked by default and revealed only to authorised roles.
sanctions.guide.rule.lifecycle: Cases advance through the defined lifecycle stages and cannot skip steps.
sanctions.guide.rule.recurrence: A case is flagged as a recurrence when the subject has a prior related sanction.
sanctions.guide.rule.appeal: An appeal can be lodged only after a disciplinary-committee decision is recorded.
sanctions.guide.tip.status: Use the status filter to build a work queue of cases still awaiting HR or DC action.
sanctions.guide.tip.recurrence: The repeat icon marks recurrences — review these first, as they often warrant harsher sanctions.
sanctions.guide.perm.hr: HR and disciplinary officers record recommendations, outcomes and appeal decisions.
sanctions.guide.perm.admin: Administrators can view every case and the unmasked subject identities.
sanctions.guide.faq.masking.q: Why do most cases show EMPLOYEE_REDACTED?
sanctions.guide.faq.masking.a: Subject identities are masked to protect employee privacy; only users with the required clearance see the real name.
sanctions.guide.faq.origin.q: How does a sanction case get created?
sanctions.guide.faq.origin.a: Cases are opened from audit findings that recommend disciplinary action; they are not created directly in this tracker.
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.purpose: See who did what and when across AuditX in one append-only, tamper-evident event log.
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.description: This is the system-wide accountability record — every significant action from every module is captured here immutably, ready to filter, review and export as audit evidence.
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.action.filter: Filter events by actor, event type, target type or date range
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.action.open: Open any event to inspect its full before/after detail
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.action.export: Export the filtered trail to a signed CSV file
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.action.verify: Verify export integrity using its SHA-256 hash
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.section.expor: Download the currently filtered events as a CSV stamped with a SHA-256 hash for tamper evidence. Needs the Export audit trail permission.
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.section.filte: Narrow the log by actor, event type, target type or date range. Filters re-query the server, so even a large history stays fast.
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.section.table: Each row is one recorded action with its time, event, actor and target. Click a row to open its full detail — entries are read-only.
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.rule.immutabl: The trail is append-only — entries are never edited or deleted, only added.
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.rule.retentio: Events are retained for the full compliance period regardless of source-record changes.
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.rule.integrit: Each CSV export carries a SHA-256 content hash so recipients can detect tampering.
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.rule.access: Viewing and exporting the trail is permission-gated and is itself recorded.
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.tip.filter: Narrow by date range and actor before exporting to keep evidence focused.
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.tip.detail: Open a row to see the full before/after payload behind an event.
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.tip.hash: Keep the SHA-256 hash alongside the exported file as proof of integrity.
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.faq.edit.q: Can I edit or delete an entry?
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.faq.edit.a: No — the trail is immutable by design. Entries can only be added, which is what makes it trustworthy evidence.
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.faq.export.q: What is the hash on an export for?
adminMisc.auditTrail.guide.faq.export.a: Each export includes a SHA-256 content hash so anyone can confirm the CSV has not been altered since it was generated.
reports.guide.purpose: Generate cross-audit reports — executive summaries, KPI packs, and registers — from analytics for download and distribution.
reports.guide.description: This page produces standalone reports that aggregate data across every audit rather than a single engagement. Pick a report kind, generate it asynchronously from the current analytics, then download or distribute the versioned, hash-sealed output to stakeholders.
reports.guide.action.generate: Generate a new standalone report of the selected kind, optionally including a DOCX rendering.
reports.guide.action.filter: Filter the list to a single report kind, or show all kinds at once.
reports.guide.action.open: Open a completed report by version to view its contents.
reports.guide.action.download: Download a completed report in any of its produced formats (PDF, DOCX, XLSX).
reports.guide.section.generate.title: Generate a report
reports.guide.section.generate.body: Choose a report kind, optionally tick 'also DOCX', and generate — the report builds in the background and appears in the list when ready.
reports.guide.section.filters.title: Filter by kind
reports.guide.section.filters.body: Narrow the history to a single report kind such as executive summary or findings register, or select All to see everything.
reports.guide.section.table.title: Report history
reports.guide.section.table.body: Every generated report is listed with its version, status, request time, and SHA-256 hash; completed rows expose download buttons per format.
reports.guide.flow.capture: Auditors capture findings, exceptions, and sanctions across engagements.
reports.guide.flow.analytics: Analytics aggregates that data into cross-audit metrics.
reports.guide.flow.generate: You generate a standalone report kind from the current analytics.
reports.guide.flow.review: The report builds asynchronously, is versioned, and sealed with a hash.
reports.guide.flow.distribute: Download or distribute the finished report to stakeholders.
reports.guide.dep.analytics: Analytics — supplies the aggregated metrics that populate each report.
reports.guide.dep.audits: Audits — the engagements whose data is rolled up across the report.
reports.guide.dep.findings: Findings & exceptions — feed the findings register and risk sections.
reports.guide.use.stakeholders: Stakeholders — receive the downloaded executive and KPI reports.
reports.guide.use.schedules: Report schedules — automate recurring generation and delivery of these kinds.
reports.guide.use.audit: Audit trail — records each generation and download for accountability.
reports.guide.rule.versioned: Each generation produces a new immutable version rather than overwriting the last.
reports.guide.rule.async: Generation runs asynchronously; the row stays pending/running until it completes or fails.
reports.guide.rule.hash: Completed reports are sealed with a SHA-256 hash so recipients can verify integrity.
reports.guide.rule.restricted: Some kinds (e.g. performance scorecards) require an extra permission to generate or open.
reports.guide.tip.docx: Tick 'also DOCX' before generating if you need an editable Word copy alongside the PDF.
reports.guide.tip.filter: Filter by kind to quickly find the latest version of a specific report.
reports.guide.tip.hash: Hover the shortened hash to copy the full SHA-256 for integrity checks.
reports.guide.perm.generate: Generate Report — required to create new standalone reports.
reports.guide.perm.view: View Report — required to open or download report contents.
reports.guide.perm.restricted: Performance Analytics View — additional permission for restricted kinds like scorecards.
reports.guide.faq.kinds.q: What kinds of standalone reports can I generate?
reports.guide.faq.kinds.a: Executive summary, annual plan status, KPI pack, audit coverage, findings register, sanctions consistency, and performance scorecards.
reports.guide.faq.pending.q: Why does my report stay in a pending or running state?
reports.guide.faq.pending.a: Reports build asynchronously; the page polls for status and the row updates to completed or failed automatically when done.
roles.guide.purpose: Define the roles and permission sets that govern what every user can see and do in AuditX.
roles.guide.description: This admin console lists all access roles — both the fixed built-in roles shipped with AuditX and any custom roles you create. Each role bundles a set of permissions and can inherit from parent roles, so access is granted consistently and least-privilege can be enforced across the whole platform.
roles.guide.action.create: Create a new custom role and assign it a tailored set of permissions.
roles.guide.action.edit: Open a role to review or edit its permissions and inheritance; built-in roles are view-only.
roles.guide.action.archive: Archive a custom role that is no longer needed to remove it from active use.
roles.guide.action.showArchived: Toggle archived roles into the list to review or reference retired roles.
roles.guide.section.create.title: New role
roles.guide.section.create.body: Start a custom role here, then pick its permissions and optional parent roles to inherit from.
roles.guide.section.toolbar.title: Show archived
roles.guide.section.toolbar.body: Flip this toggle to include archived roles in the table alongside the active ones.
roles.guide.section.table.title: Roles table
roles.guide.section.table.body: Every role with its description, permission count and type badges (built-in, archived, inherits); click a row to open it.
roles.guide.flow.define: Define a role with a clear name and purpose.
roles.guide.flow.permissions: Select the permissions from the catalogue that the role should grant.
roles.guide.flow.inherit: Optionally set parent roles so the role inherits their permissions.
roles.guide.flow.assign: Assign the role to users in the identity module.
roles.guide.flow.enforce: AuditX enforces the resolved permissions on every screen and action.
roles.guide.dep.permissions: The permission catalogue that supplies the grantable capabilities.
roles.guide.dep.builtin: Built-in system roles that ship with AuditX as a baseline.
roles.guide.dep.parents: Parent roles referenced for hierarchical permission inheritance.
roles.guide.use.users: User accounts are assigned roles to receive their access rights.
roles.guide.use.audits: Audit, plan and finding actions are gated by the permissions these roles grant.
roles.guide.use.access: Menu visibility and platform-wide access control resolve from a user's roles.
roles.guide.rule.builtin: Built-in roles cannot be edited or archived; open them to view only.
roles.guide.rule.inherit: A role's effective permissions are its own plus all those inherited from its parent roles.
roles.guide.rule.archive: Archiving hides a role from active use without deleting its history.
roles.guide.rule.assigned: Review user assignments before archiving a role so no one loses required access.
roles.guide.tip.inherit: Use parent roles to compose permissions once and reuse them across many roles.
roles.guide.tip.least: Grant the minimum permissions needed to honour least-privilege access.
roles.guide.tip.showArchived: Turn on Show archived to audit or restore previously retired roles.
roles.guide.perm.admin: Administrators can create, edit and archive custom roles and their permissions.
roles.guide.perm.viewer: Other users may view roles but cannot modify the permission catalogue.
roles.guide.faq.builtin.q: Why can't I edit a built-in role?
roles.guide.faq.builtin.a: Built-in roles are system-defined baselines; to change access, create a custom role instead or adjust the role assigned to the user.
roles.guide.faq.inherit.a: When a role lists parent roles, it automatically receives all of their permissions in addition to its own, so shared access only needs to be defined once.
compliance.guide.purpose: Maintain the register of regulations and standards that audit findings and controls are mapped to for compliance reporting.
compliance.guide.description: The regulation register is the authoritative catalogue of the external regulations, laws, and standards your organisation is held to. Each entry records a unique code, the issuing authority, and a category, giving findings and controls a stable reference to map against so compliance coverage can be measured and reported.
compliance.guide.action.register: Register a new regulation or standard with its code, authority, and category.
compliance.guide.action.filter: Filter the register by category, free-text search, or include retired entries.
compliance.guide.action.edit: Edit an existing regulation's details to keep the register accurate.
compliance.guide.action.retire: Retire (deactivate) or delete a regulation that no longer applies.
compliance.guide.section.register.title: Register a regulation
compliance.guide.section.register.body: Use this button to add a new regulation or standard to the register; it is available only to users who can manage the compliance library.
compliance.guide.section.filters.title: Filter the register
compliance.guide.section.filters.body: Search by name or code, narrow by category, and toggle whether retired regulations appear in the list.
compliance.guide.section.table.title: Regulation list
compliance.guide.section.table.body: Each row shows a regulation's code, name, issuing authority, category, and active status, with a menu to edit, retire, or delete it.
compliance.guide.flow.identify: Identify the regulations and standards your organisation must comply with.
compliance.guide.flow.register: Register each one here with a unique code, authority, and category.
compliance.guide.flow.map: Map audit findings and controls to the relevant regulations.
compliance.guide.flow.assess: Assess compliance coverage across mapped findings and controls.
compliance.guide.flow.report: Report on regulatory compliance using the register as the reference set.
compliance.guide.dep.authority: The issuing authority (e.g. regulator or standards body) that owns each regulation.
compliance.guide.dep.category: A category taxonomy used to group and filter regulations.
compliance.guide.dep.permission: The manage-controls permission, which gates registering and editing entries.
compliance.guide.use.findings: Audit findings reference regulations to flag compliance breaches.
compliance.guide.use.controls: Controls are mapped to regulations to demonstrate coverage.
compliance.guide.use.reports: Compliance reports and analytics aggregate coverage against the register.
compliance.guide.rule.code: Each regulation must have a code that is unique within the register.
compliance.guide.rule.retire: Retiring a regulation deactivates it but preserves existing mappings and history.
compliance.guide.rule.delete: A regulation can only be deleted when it is not referenced by findings or controls.
compliance.guide.rule.version: Edits use optimistic concurrency, so a stale version is rejected to prevent overwrites.
compliance.guide.tip.authority: Record the issuing authority so reports can be grouped by regulator.
compliance.guide.tip.category: Use consistent categories to make the register easy to filter and report on.
compliance.guide.tip.retire: Prefer retiring over deleting to keep an audit trail of superseded regulations.
compliance.guide.perm.manage: Compliance managers can register, edit, retire, and delete regulations.
compliance.guide.perm.view: Other users with access can view and filter the register but not change it.
compliance.guide.faq.retireDelete.q: What is the difference between retiring and deleting a regulation?
compliance.guide.faq.retireDelete.a: Retiring keeps the regulation and its mappings for historical reporting but marks it inactive, while deleting removes it entirely and is only allowed when nothing references it.
compliance.guide.faq.mapping.q: How do regulations connect to audits?
compliance.guide.faq.mapping.a: Findings and controls are mapped to regulations in this register, which lets compliance reports measure how well each regulation is covered.
trends.guide.purpose: Track how a KPI moves over time and compare each period against the one before, with a simple forecast of what comes next.
trends.guide.description: This view charts a chosen audit metric from the daily analytics snapshots, buckets it by month, quarter or year, shows the latest-versus-previous change, and projects the next period so you can spot trends early.
trends.guide.action.metric: Choose which KPI metric to analyse from the snapshot library
trends.guide.action.period: Switch the comparison grain between month, quarter and year
trends.guide.action.forecast: Read the latest-versus-previous delta and the projected next-period value
trends.guide.action.refresh: Refresh the trend from the latest snapshots, or return to all dashboards
trends.guide.section.controls.title: Pick a metric & grain
trends.guide.section.controls.body: Select the KPI to analyse and the comparison grain (month, quarter or year); each change re-queries the snapshot history.
trends.guide.section.stats.title: Comparison & forecast
trends.guide.section.stats.body: The current and previous period values, the change between them with direction, and a linear forecast for the next period.
trends.guide.section.chart.title: Trend chart
trends.guide.section.chart.body: The trailing period buckets plotted as a line so you can see the shape of the trend; missing buckets are skipped.
trends.guide.rule.snapshot: Values come from point-in-time daily snapshots, so history only exists from when snapshot capture began.
trends.guide.rule.forecast: The forecast is a straight-line projection from recent buckets — a guide, not a guarantee.
trends.guide.rule.series: At least two valued periods are needed before a change and forecast can be shown.
trends.guide.rule.grain: Changing the grain re-buckets the same underlying snapshots — month, quarter and year share one source.
trends.guide.tip.grain: Use a longer grain (quarter or year) to smooth out noisy day-to-day movement.
trends.guide.tip.metric: Compare related metrics — for example open backlog against closure rate — to explain a trend.
trends.guide.tip.delta: Watch the delta direction: an up arrow is not always good — for backlog or open exceptions, down is better.
trends.guide.faq.empty.q: Why is there no trend to show?
trends.guide.faq.empty.a: The metric needs at least two periods with captured snapshot values; newly seeded environments build up history over time.
trends.guide.faq.forecast.a: It is a simple linear projection of the recent period buckets onto the next period — treat it as an indicative trend, not a target.
reportSchedules.guide.purpose: Set up recurring standalone reports that generate and email themselves on a fixed cadence.
reportSchedules.guide.description: The report-schedules admin lets you automate cross-audit reporting: pick a report type, choose how often it runs, and add the people who should receive it. Each schedule auto-generates its report on the next run date and emails it to the chosen recipients, so leadership and stakeholders get their packs without anyone remembering to run them.
reportSchedules.guide.action.new: Create a schedule — pick a report kind, cadence, and recipients.
reportSchedules.guide.action.edit: Edit a schedule's name, cadence, or recipient list.
reportSchedules.guide.action.pause: Pause a schedule so it stops generating, then reactivate it later.
reportSchedules.guide.action.delete: Delete a schedule you no longer need.
reportSchedules.guide.section.create.bod: Opens the schedule dialog where you choose the report kind, cadence, and recipients. Requires the Schedule Reports permission.
reportSchedules.guide.section.table.body: Each row shows a schedule's report kind, cadence, recipient count, next run date, and active/paused status, with a row menu to edit or delete it.
reportSchedules.guide.section.status.bod: Active schedules run on their next run date; paused ones are held and show no next run until you reactivate them.
reportSchedules.guide.flow.pick: Choose which standalone report kind to schedule.
reportSchedules.guide.flow.cadence: Set the cadence — daily, weekly, monthly, or quarterly.
reportSchedules.guide.flow.recipients: Add recipients from your users plus any ad-hoc email addresses.
reportSchedules.guide.flow.generate: On the next run date the scheduler auto-generates the report.
reportSchedules.guide.flow.deliver: The finished report is emailed to every recipient.
reportSchedules.guide.dep.reports: Standalone reports — the report kinds this schedule can generate.
reportSchedules.guide.dep.users: Users — the directory backing the recipient picker.
reportSchedules.guide.dep.email: Email delivery — the channel used to send generated reports.
reportSchedules.guide.use.recipients: Recipients — users and mailboxes that receive the delivered reports.
reportSchedules.guide.use.reports: Standalone reports — each run produces a report in the reports library.
reportSchedules.guide.use.audit: Audit trail — schedule changes and deliveries are recorded for oversight.
reportSchedules.guide.rule.kind: The report kind is fixed at creation and cannot be changed on an existing schedule.
reportSchedules.guide.rule.pause: Pausing a schedule stops future runs and clears its next run date until reactivated.
reportSchedules.guide.rule.recipients: A schedule needs at least one recipient — a directory user or an ad-hoc email.
reportSchedules.guide.rule.nextRun: The next run date is derived from the cadence and advances automatically after each run.
reportSchedules.guide.tip.email: Use ad-hoc email addresses for external stakeholders who don't have AuditX accounts.
reportSchedules.guide.tip.pause: Pause rather than delete a schedule during quiet periods so you keep its configuration.
reportSchedules.guide.perm.manage: Users with Schedule Reports can create, edit, pause, and delete schedules.
reportSchedules.guide.perm.view: Other users can view the schedules list but cannot change it.
reportSchedules.guide.faq.when.q: When does a scheduled report actually run?
reportSchedules.guide.faq.when.a: On the schedule's next run date, which the scheduler derives from its cadence and advances after each successful run.
reportSchedules.guide.faq.kind.q: Can I change the report type of an existing schedule?
reportSchedules.guide.faq.kind.a: No — the report kind is set when you create the schedule. Delete it and create a new one to switch report types.
referenceData.guide.title: Reference data
referenceData.guide.purpose: Maintain the organization-configurable lookup lists that populate dropdowns across AuditX.
referenceData.guide.description: This is the admin home for keyed reference lists — audit types, exception categories, document types and more. Curate each category's items so every module offers consistent, organization-approved choices.
referenceData.guide.action.select: Select a category to view and manage its items
referenceData.guide.action.create: Add a new item to the selected category
referenceData.guide.action.edit: Edit an item's label, description or sort order
referenceData.guide.action.archive: Archive or reactivate items to control what appears in dropdowns
referenceData.guide.section.create.title: Add an item
referenceData.guide.section.create.body: Create a new entry in the selected category — it becomes available in the matching dropdowns app-wide. Needs the Manage configuration permission.
referenceData.guide.section.filters.body: Pick which reference list you're editing, and toggle Show inactive to reveal archived items for review or reactivation.
referenceData.guide.section.table.title: The item list
referenceData.guide.section.table.body: Each item with its code, label, description, sort order and status. Use the row actions to edit, archive or reactivate.
referenceData.guide.rule.code: Each item is identified by a unique code within its category, used to link it across the app.
referenceData.guide.rule.archive: Archiving hides an item from dropdowns but keeps records that already reference it intact — it is never hard-deleted.
referenceData.guide.rule.sort: Sort order controls the sequence items appear in throughout the app's dropdowns.
referenceData.guide.rule.permission: Only users with the Manage configuration permission can create, edit or archive items.
referenceData.guide.tip.inactive: Turn on Show inactive to find and reactivate a previously archived item.
referenceData.guide.tip.sort: Give common choices a lower sort order so they surface first in dropdowns.
referenceData.guide.tip.archive: Archive instead of deleting to retire a choice while preserving historical records.
referenceData.guide.faq.edit.q: Why can't I add or edit items?
referenceData.guide.faq.edit.a: Managing reference data needs the Manage configuration permission, which is typically held by Administrators.
referenceData.guide.faq.archive.q: What happens when I archive an item?
referenceData.guide.faq.archive.a: It stops appearing in dropdowns from then on, but existing records that already use it are unaffected — you can reactivate it anytime.
notifications.guide.purpose: Configure how AuditX turns domain events into email and SMS alerts, and monitor their delivery.
notifications.guide.description: The notifications admin is where you define event-driven rules and message templates, watch every delivery in the dispatch log, and redrive sends that landed in the dead-letter queue. It keeps auditors, managers and stakeholders informed the moment an audit, finding or report event fires.
notifications.guide.action.configure: Define event-to-notification rules that bind an event type to a template, channels and recipients.
notifications.guide.action.templates: Author organisation email and SMS templates, or override the system defaults.
notifications.guide.action.monitor: Track every delivery attempt in the dispatch log by status, channel and recipient.
notifications.guide.action.redrive: Retry dispatches that reached the dead-letter queue after exhausting automatic retries.
notifications.guide.section.tabs.title: Rules, templates, log and dead-letter
notifications.guide.section.tabs.body: Four tabs organise the workspace: configure Rules and Templates, watch the Dispatch Log, and redrive the Dead-letter queue.
notifications.guide.section.toolbar.body: Add a new event-driven rule or refresh the list; each rule maps an event type to a template, delivery channels and recipients.
notifications.guide.section.table.title: Configured rules
notifications.guide.section.table.body: Lists every rule with its event, channels and recipients — preview the resolved message, edit, or deactivate a rule from here.
notifications.guide.flow.event: A module raises a domain event, such as an audit created, a finding overdue, or a report ready.
notifications.guide.flow.match: The engine matches the event against the active notification rules.
notifications.guide.flow.resolve: Recipients are resolved and the template is rendered for each channel.
notifications.guide.flow.dispatch: The message is dispatched by email or SMS and recorded in the dispatch log.
notifications.guide.flow.retry: Failed sends retry automatically and move to the dead-letter queue once exhausted.
notifications.guide.dep.events: Domain events emitted across AuditX modules that trigger notifications.
notifications.guide.dep.templates: Email and SMS templates that supply the rendered message content.
notifications.guide.dep.users: The identity directory used to resolve rule recipients.
notifications.guide.dep.providers: The configured email and SMS delivery providers.
notifications.guide.use.recipients: Auditors, managers and stakeholders who receive the alerts.
notifications.guide.use.audits: Audit and finding workflows that depend on timely follow-up.
notifications.guide.use.schedules: Recurring report schedules that deliver output by email.
notifications.guide.use.auditTrail: The audit trail, which records every rule and template change.
notifications.guide.rule.systemDefault: System-default rules and templates are read-only; organisations override them with their own copy.
notifications.guide.rule.channels: Every rule must specify at least one delivery channel — email or SMS.
notifications.guide.rule.recipients: A rule needs a recipient-resolution definition, or nothing is sent.
notifications.guide.rule.deadLetter: A dispatch is dead-lettered only after its automatic retries are exhausted.
notifications.guide.tip.preview: Use Preview to check the resolved recipients and rendered message before relying on a rule.
notifications.guide.tip.filter: Filter the dispatch log by status and event type to isolate failures quickly.
notifications.guide.tip.redrive: Fix the underlying template or provider issue before retrying dead-lettered dispatches.
notifications.guide.perm.configure: Configure Notifications lets an administrator create and edit rules and templates.
notifications.guide.perm.ops: Admin Ops is required to retry dispatches from the dead-letter queue.
notifications.guide.perm.view: Other admins can view the dispatch log and preview rules without editing.
notifications.guide.faq.trigger.q: Why didn't a notification go out?
notifications.guide.faq.trigger.a: Check the dispatch log and dead-letter queue — a missing active rule, unresolved recipients, or a provider failure are the usual causes.
notifications.guide.faq.sms.q: How do email and SMS differ?
notifications.guide.faq.sms.a: Each rule can target either or both channels; SMS uses a shorter template and requires a mobile number on the recipient.
integrations.guide.purpose: Configure and monitor the outbound integrations and webhooks that connect AuditX to external systems.
integrations.guide.description: This is the admin console for integrations — register webhook, email, SIEM and identity connectors, test their connectivity, and monitor each one's health from a single register.
integrations.guide.action.create: Register a new integration or outbound webhook
integrations.guide.action.test: Send a test call to verify an endpoint's connectivity
integrations.guide.action.edit: Edit an integration's endpoint and configuration
integrations.guide.action.deactivate: Deactivate an integration to stop its traffic
integrations.guide.section.create.title: Add an integration
integrations.guide.section.create.body: Register a new webhook, SMTP, SIEM or identity connector here. Needs the Configure integrations permission.
integrations.guide.section.table.title: The integration register
integrations.guide.section.table.body: Every configured integration with its type, health and active status. Use the row menu to test, edit or deactivate.
integrations.guide.section.health.title: Health & status
integrations.guide.section.health.body: The health badge shows healthy, degraded or failing from the last check; the status badge shows whether the integration is active.
integrations.guide.rule.primary: Only one integration of each type can be marked primary and used by the platform.
integrations.guide.rule.test: Test an integration before activating it to confirm the endpoint and credentials work.
integrations.guide.rule.deactivate: Deactivating an integration stops its traffic immediately but keeps its configuration.
integrations.guide.rule.health: Health is polled best-effort; a failing state signals recent delivery errors.
integrations.guide.tip.test: Run a test after every configuration change to catch endpoint errors early.
integrations.guide.tip.health: Watch the health column — a degraded badge often precedes a full outage.
integrations.guide.tip.primary: Mark one integration primary per type so the platform knows which to use.
integrations.guide.faq.manage.q: Why can't I add or edit an integration?
integrations.guide.faq.manage.a: Managing integrations needs the Configure integrations permission, held by Administrators.
integrations.guide.faq.health.q: What do the health states mean?
integrations.guide.faq.health.a: Healthy means recent calls succeeded, degraded means intermittent errors, and failing means the last checks did not connect.
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.purpose: See where enterprise risk concentrates by scoring every open risk on likelihood and impact.
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.description: A 5x5 heat-map of the enterprise risk register — each open risk is plotted by its likelihood and impact so you can spot concentrations, brief management, and steer audit focus toward the highest-scoring cells.
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.action.read: Read where open risks concentrate across the likelihood x impact grid
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.action.summa: Review register totals — open risks, overdue reviews and counts by severity band
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.action.regis: Open the full risk register to inspect or update individual risks
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.action.refre: Refresh the map with the latest register data
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.section.summ: Headline counts for the register — open risks, reviews now overdue, and a tally by severity band.
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.section.grid: Each cell is a likelihood x impact combination; the number is how many open risks land there and the colour is its severity band. Hover a cell for its score and count.
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.section.regi: Jump to the full register to drill into individual risks, edit assessments or record treatment.
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.rule.score: A risk's score is likelihood x impact (1–25), which decides its heat-map cell.
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.rule.open: Only open risks are plotted — closed or accepted risks drop off the map.
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.rule.band: Cell colour follows the severity band derived from the score, not the raw number.
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.rule.overdue: A risk is flagged overdue when its next review date has passed.
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.tip.corner: The top-right cells (high likelihood, high impact) are your critical risks — start there.
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.tip.hover: Hover any cell to see its likelihood, impact, score and risk count.
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.tip.act: Faintly tinted cells hold no open risks; act on the populated, darker ones.
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.faq.empty.a: There are no open risks in the register yet — add or reopen risks and they will appear on the grid.
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.faq.colour.q: What do the cell colours mean?
analytics.riskHeatmap.guide.faq.colour.a: Each colour is a severity band (low to critical) from the likelihood x impact score; darker, filled cells hold open risks.
analytics.controlsCompliance.guide.purpo: See how well your controls are working and how you are tracking against each regulation.
analytics.controlsCompliance.guide.descr: This view rolls up control-effectiveness testing across the register and maps open exceptions to the regulations they breach, giving one read on assurance and compliance health.
analytics.controlsCompliance.guide.actio: Review the control-effectiveness roll-up and effective share
Break controls down by effectiveness rating and control type
Scan compliance by regulation with linked and open findings
Refresh the analytics to pull the latest results
analytics.controlsCompliance.guide.secti: Headline KPIs — active controls, how many were tested, ineffective count, and the effective share over tested controls.
Counts by effectiveness rating and by control type, so you can see where assurance is weak.
Each regulation with its authority, findings linked to it, and how many of those are still open.
The effective share is calculated over tested controls only, so untested controls never inflate or deflate it.
Only active controls are counted in the effectiveness roll-up.
A regulation's open count includes only findings that are linked to it and not yet resolved.
analytics.controlsCompliance.guide.tip.i: Start with regulations that have open findings and controls rated ineffective — that is where risk is concentrated.
analytics.controlsCompliance.guide.tip.r: Use the register link to jump to the controls list and update ratings or evidence.
analytics.controlsCompliance.guide.faq.s: Why is the effective share missing?
It only appears once at least one control has been tested; with zero tested controls there is nothing to divide by.
analytics.controlsCompliance.guide.faq.e: Why is the compliance table empty?
No regulations have findings linked to them yet — map exceptions to regulations to populate this table.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.purpose: Ranks every department and business unit by audit activity, open findings, and remediation speed, rolled up the org hierarchy.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.descriptio: Each row aggregates an org unit plus all of its descendants, so leaders can see where audit risk concentrates and which units close findings fastest.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.action.rev: Review findings, completed audits, and closure speed for each org unit.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.action.com: Compare departments side by side on open, critical, and high-severity findings.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.action.dri: Read the indented hierarchy to see how a parent unit's totals break down by sub-unit.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.action.ref: Refresh to pull the latest aggregates after audits or findings change.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.section.su: Totals for units, entities, open findings, and open criticals, summed over root units only to avoid double-counting nested subtrees.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.section.ta: One row per org unit with entities, audits completed and in flight, open/critical/high/closed findings, and average closure days.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.section.hi: The unit name is indented by its depth so parent units and their nested sub-units read as a tree.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.flow.assig: Entities and audits are assigned to org units in the audit universe.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.flow.audit: Audits run against those units and record findings.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.flow.findi: Findings accrue severity and closure dates as remediation progresses.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.flow.rollu: Metrics roll up each unit's whole subtree into a scorecard row.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.flow.act: Leadership acts on the ranking to reprioritise audits and remediation.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.dep.orgUni: Org units define the hierarchy that rows are grouped and rolled up by.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.dep.audits: Audits supply the completed and in-flight counts per unit.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.dep.findin: Findings supply the open, critical, high, closed, and closure-day metrics.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.use.leader: Leadership uses the ranking to spot high-risk departments at a glance.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.use.planni: Audit planning targets units with weak closure rates or many open findings.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.use.report: Cross-audit reports and dashboards cite these org-unit aggregates.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.rule.rollu: Each row aggregates the org unit plus all of its descendant units.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.rule.summa: The summary strip sums root units only, since each root already rolls up its subtree.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.rule.closu: Average closure days is computed from closed findings only; units with none show a dash.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.tip.critic: Watch the critical-open badge — any non-zero value flags a unit needing immediate attention.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.tip.indent: Deeper indentation means a sub-unit; its numbers are already included in its parent's row.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.perm.view: Requires the ViewAnalytics permission to open this dashboard.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.perm.orgUn: Org-unit hierarchy must be configured for units to appear and roll up.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.faq.rollup: Why do a parent unit's totals exceed the sum of the rows shown under it?
Each row already includes its entire subtree, so a parent's totals cover descendants that may also appear as their own rows.
analytics.orgScorecards.guide.faq.closur: What does a dash in the average closure days column mean?
That unit has no closed findings yet, so there is no closure time to average.
analytics.performanceScorecards.guide.pu: Rank each audit lead on throughput, cycle time, and how well they raise and close exceptions.
analytics.performanceScorecards.guide.de: This leaderboard aggregates completed and in-flight audits per lead — audits led, audits completed, average end-to-end cycle days, exceptions raised, exceptions closed, and average exception closure days — so managers can benchmark delivery and resolution speed across the team.
analytics.performanceScorecards.guide.ac: Review each lead's audit volume and completion count at a glance.
Compare average cycle and closure days to spot fast and slow performers.
Drill into individual audits or findings to explain an outlier metric.
Refresh to pull the latest completion and closure figures.
analytics.performanceScorecards.guide.se: Return to the analytics hub or refresh the scorecard to recompute the latest per-lead metrics.
One row per audit lead, resolved from user IDs to names, ordered so you can benchmark the whole team side by side.
Columns cover audits led and completed, average cycle days, and exceptions raised, closed, and their average closure days.
analytics.performanceScorecards.guide.fl: A user is assigned as lead on an audit.
The audit progresses through its lifecycle and is completed.
Findings and exceptions are raised and later closed during fieldwork.
AuditX rolls the counts and elapsed days up per lead.
Managers review the scorecard to appraise and balance workload.
analytics.performanceScorecards.guide.de: Audits with an assigned lead, completion dates, and cycle timing.
Findings/exceptions with raised and closed timestamps per audit.
The user directory that resolves lead IDs to display names.
analytics.performanceScorecards.guide.us: Performance appraisals and one-on-one coaching for audit leads.
Capacity and workload planning across the audit team.
Standalone performance-scorecard reports exported for management.
analytics.performanceScorecards.guide.ru: Only users assigned as an audit lead appear as a row.
Audits completed counts only audits that reached the completed status.
Average cycle days measures elapsed time from audit start to completion.
Average closure days measures elapsed time from an exception being raised to closed.
analytics.performanceScorecards.guide.ti: Read cycle and closure days alongside volume — a low count can flatter the averages.
A high raised-versus-closed gap flags a lead carrying open exceptions.
analytics.performanceScorecards.guide.pe: Requires the PerformanceAnalyticsView permission to open this page.
Per-auditor performance is sensitive — access is limited to managers and administrators.
analytics.performanceScorecards.guide.fa: No audits have an assigned lead yet, or none have progressed far enough to produce metrics.
How should I read the averages?
Cycle and closure days are averages, so weigh them against audits led and exceptions raised before ranking a lead.
analytics.timeBudget.guide.purpose: See where audit hours are budgeted, spent and how each auditor's time splits across engagements.
analytics.timeBudget.guide.description: This dashboard turns logged time entries into two views: budget-vs-actual hours per audit and utilisation per auditor, so managers can catch overruns early and balance workload.
analytics.timeBudget.guide.action.budget: Compare budgeted versus actual hours and variance per audit
analytics.timeBudget.guide.action.utilis: Review total hours and workload split per auditor
analytics.timeBudget.guide.action.open: Read the lead, status and percent-consumed for each engagement
analytics.timeBudget.guide.action.refres: Refresh the figures after new time entries are logged
analytics.timeBudget.guide.section.budge: Each audit's budgeted hours, actual hours, variance and percent consumed. A negative variance (highlighted) means the audit is over budget.
analytics.timeBudget.guide.section.utili: Total hours per auditor, how many audits they contributed to, and a split of hours by time category such as fieldwork or review.
analytics.timeBudget.guide.section.refre: Recompute both tables on demand — useful right after auditors log or adjust their time entries.
analytics.timeBudget.guide.rule.variance: Variance is budgeted minus actual hours; a negative value flags an over-budget audit.
analytics.timeBudget.guide.rule.consumed: Percent consumed compares actual against budgeted hours and needs a budget to be set.
analytics.timeBudget.guide.rule.utilisat: Utilisation totals only count approved time entries attributed to an auditor.
analytics.timeBudget.guide.tip.over: Scan the variance column for negative values to spot overruns before they escalate.
analytics.timeBudget.guide.tip.split: Use the category split to see whether time is going into fieldwork or review.
analytics.timeBudget.guide.faq.empty.a: No time entries have been logged yet, or none match the current audits — figures appear once auditors record their hours.
Why is a budget or variance shown as a dash?
That audit has no budgeted hours set, so variance and percent consumed cannot be calculated.
analytics.workload.title: Auditor workload
analytics.workload.subtitle: Open planned effort per lead against declared capacity.
analytics.workload.empty.title: No workload to show
analytics.workload.empty.message: No auditor has open planned work or a declared capacity yet. Assign leads to plan items and set capacities to populate this view.
analytics.workload.guide.purpose: See how open planned work is distributed across auditors, so over- and under-committed leads can be re-balanced before the plan runs.
analytics.workload.guide.description: This page rolls up the estimated effort of open plan items (Planned or In progress) by their assigned lead, and compares each lead's total against the capacity declared on their user profile. Over-committed auditors are flagged so work can be reassigned; auditors with capacity but little load surface as spare resource.
analytics.workload.guide.action.scan: Scan the table for over-committed leads (utilisation above 100%).
analytics.workload.guide.action.capacity: Set an auditor's capacity from their user profile to make utilisation meaningful.
analytics.workload.guide.action.refresh: Refresh to pick up newly assigned plan items or capacity changes.
analytics.workload.guide.section.table.b: One row per auditor: open item count, total planned days, declared capacity, utilisation, and whether they are within or over capacity.
analytics.workload.guide.section.refresh: Re-runs the roll-up. The numbers reflect the current plan-item assignments and user capacities.
analytics.workload.guide.flow.capacity: Set each auditor's annual capacity on their profile.
analytics.workload.guide.flow.plan: Estimate effort on plan items during annual planning.
analytics.workload.guide.flow.assign: Assign a lead auditor to each plan item.
analytics.workload.guide.flow.aggregate: This page aggregates open planned effort by lead.
analytics.workload.guide.flow.rebalance: Re-balance assignments where a lead is over-committed.
analytics.workload.guide.dep.plans: Annual plan items (estimated effort + assigned lead).
analytics.workload.guide.rule.open: Only open plan items (Planned or In progress) count toward the load; completed and deferred items are excluded.
analytics.workload.guide.rule.utilisatio: Utilisation = planned days ÷ capacity days × 100. It is blank until a capacity is declared.
analytics.workload.guide.rule.over: A lead is over-committed when their planned days exceed their declared capacity.
analytics.workload.guide.tip.capacity: An auditor with no capacity set still appears (with their planned load) so you can add one.
analytics.workload.guide.tip.over: Over-committed rows highlight the utilisation figure in red.
analytics.workload.guide.perm.analytics: View analytics — to open this page.
analytics.workload.guide.perm.manage: Manage users — to set an auditor's capacity.
analytics.workload.guide.faq.capacity.q: Why is utilisation blank for an auditor?
analytics.workload.guide.faq.capacity.a: No capacity has been declared on that user's profile. Set one (Manage users) and the utilisation and over/under-capacity status will appear.
analytics.workload.guide.faq.open.q: Why doesn't a completed audit's effort show here?
analytics.workload.guide.faq.open.a: This view is forward-looking: it only sums open plan items (Planned or In progress). Completed and deferred items no longer represent outstanding load.
analytics.throughput.title: Auditor throughput
analytics.throughput.subtitle: Hands-on audit work per team member — not just leads.
analytics.throughput.empty.title: No throughput to show
analytics.throughput.empty.message: No checklist responses, evidence, or findings have been recorded by team members yet.
analytics.throughput.guide.purpose: See how hands-on audit work is distributed across the whole team — every auditor's responses, evidence and findings, not only the engagement leads.
analytics.throughput.guide.description: The lead-only performance scorecards miss the contribution of non-lead auditors and reviewers. This view counts each user's finalised checklist responses, evidence uploads, findings raised, and checklist items assigned, so you can gauge individual contribution and spot under- or over-loaded team members. Figures are personnel-sensitive; your own row is hidden unless you hold audit-committee oversight.
analytics.throughput.guide.action.review: Review each auditor's finalised responses, evidence and findings.
analytics.throughput.guide.action.compar: Compare contribution across the team, sorted by hands-on volume.
analytics.throughput.guide.action.refres: Refresh to pick up newly recorded work.
analytics.throughput.guide.section.contr: Return to the analytics hub or refresh the throughput table.
analytics.throughput.guide.section.table: One row per team member: finalised responses, evidence uploaded, findings raised, and items assigned. Sorted by total hands-on volume.
analytics.throughput.guide.flow.respond: Auditors record finalised responses on checklist items.
analytics.throughput.guide.flow.evidence: They upload evidence to support their work.
analytics.throughput.guide.flow.raise: They raise findings on failed items.
analytics.throughput.guide.flow.aggregat: This view aggregates that work per user.
analytics.throughput.guide.flow.review: Managers review contribution for appraisal and balancing.
analytics.throughput.guide.dep.exception: Findings (by the auditor who raised them).
analytics.throughput.guide.use.capacity: Balancing hands-on load across the team.
analytics.throughput.guide.rule.team: Counts every team member's work, not just engagement leads.
analytics.throughput.guide.rule.finalise: Only finalised (non-draft) checklist responses count toward the responded total.
analytics.throughput.guide.rule.self: Your own row is suppressed unless you hold audit-committee (CIA) oversight.
analytics.throughput.guide.tip.context: High response counts don't equal quality — read alongside the findings raised.
analytics.throughput.guide.tip.lead: For lead-level cycle-time and closure metrics, see the performance scorecards.
analytics.throughput.guide.perm.view: Performance analytics view — to open this page.
analytics.throughput.guide.perm.self: Audit-committee oversight (CIA) — to include your own row.
analytics.throughput.guide.faq.self.q: Why isn't my own row shown?
analytics.throughput.guide.faq.self.a: Auditors cannot grade their own throughput: your row is suppressed unless you additionally hold audit-committee (CIA) oversight.
analytics.throughput.guide.faq.lead.q: How is this different from performance scorecards?
analytics.throughput.guide.faq.lead.a: Performance scorecards summarise the engagement LEAD (cycle time, closure). This view counts hands-on work by EVERY team member, so non-lead auditors and reviewers are represented too.
analytics.recurrence.guide.purpose: Surface entities where the same kind of closed finding keeps coming back, so systemic issues get attention.
analytics.recurrence.guide.description: This page lists clusters of recurring or similar findings detected across audits. Each row groups closed exceptions for one auditable entity and category over a rolling window, showing how many times the issue recurred, when it last happened, and when the cluster was detected. Drill into a row to see the member findings and decide whether a deeper, root-cause response is warranted.
analytics.recurrence.guide.action.scan: Scan the table for entities with high recurrence counts.
analytics.recurrence.guide.action.drill: Open a cluster to review its member findings and audits.
analytics.recurrence.guide.action.refres: Refresh to re-run detection against the latest closed findings.
analytics.recurrence.guide.action.act: Escalate systemic clusters into risks or follow-up audits.
analytics.recurrence.guide.section.refre: Re-runs the recurrence scan so newly closed findings are reflected in the clusters below.
analytics.recurrence.guide.section.table: Each row is a cluster for one entity and category: recurring closed-finding count, the rolling window in months, last occurrence, and detection date. Use View to drill into the member findings.
analytics.recurrence.guide.section.pagin: Page through the full set of detected clusters and adjust how many appear per page.
analytics.recurrence.guide.flow.detect: Recurrence detection groups similar closed findings
analytics.recurrence.guide.flow.act: Systemic clusters drive risks and follow-up audits
analytics.recurrence.guide.dep.findings: Closed findings (exceptions) that supply the recurrence signal.
analytics.recurrence.guide.dep.entities: Auditable entities that clusters are grouped and named by.
analytics.recurrence.guide.dep.audits: Audits in which the member findings were raised.
analytics.recurrence.guide.use.risks: Risk register — recurring issues justify new or elevated risks.
analytics.recurrence.guide.use.planning: Audit planning — repeat offenders warrant added coverage.
analytics.recurrence.guide.use.reports: Reports and dashboards that highlight systemic themes.
analytics.recurrence.guide.rule.closed: Only closed findings feed a cluster, so recurrence reflects resolved-yet-repeating issues.
analytics.recurrence.guide.rule.window: Clusters are measured over a rolling window (in months) per entity and category.
analytics.recurrence.guide.rule.grouping: Findings are grouped by auditable entity and category to identify a genuine pattern.
analytics.recurrence.guide.tip.drill: Open a cluster before acting — the member findings show whether the recurrence is truly the same issue.
analytics.recurrence.guide.tip.systemic: A rising recurrence count usually signals a control weakness rather than isolated one-off exceptions.
analytics.recurrence.guide.perm.view: ViewAnalytics — required to open this page and its clusters.
analytics.recurrence.guide.perm.performa: PerformanceAnalyticsView — grants the wider analytics dashboards this page sits within.
analytics.recurrence.guide.faq.what.q: What counts as a recurrence cluster?
analytics.recurrence.guide.faq.what.a: A group of closed findings of the same category that repeat for one auditable entity within the detection window.
analytics.recurrence.guide.faq.window.q: What does the window column mean?
analytics.recurrence.guide.faq.window.a: It is the rolling look-back period, in months, over which the repeating findings were counted.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.purpose: Browse the analytics dashboards you may see and open one to review its widgets.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.descripti: This page lists every configurable analytics dashboard available to you as a navigable card, showing its name, slug and visible-widget count. Open a dashboard to read its assembled charts and KPIs, or build a custom one to focus a specific audience on the metrics that matter.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.action.op: Open a dashboard card to view its widgets and metrics.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.action.bu: Build or configure a custom dashboard from available widgets.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.action.cl: Jump to recurrence clusters to explore repeat-finding themes.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.action.re: Refresh the list to pick up newly published dashboards.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.section.a: Shortcuts to the recurrence-clusters view and a refresh that reloads the dashboard list.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.section.g: Every dashboard you have permission to see is laid out here as a card; an empty grid means none are configured or visible to you.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.section.c: Each card shows a dashboard's name, slug and widget count; click it to open the dashboard by its unique slug.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.flow.capt: Audits, findings and risks generate operational data.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.flow.snap: Analytics snapshots aggregate that data into metrics.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.flow.comp: Dashboards bundle widgets over those metrics.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.flow.brow: Browse this list and open the dashboard you need.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.flow.act: Read the widgets and drill into the underlying records.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.dep.snaps: Analytics snapshot data aggregated from operational modules.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.dep.modul: Audit, finding, risk and control data feeding the metrics.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.dep.permi: A ViewAnalytics grant to see any dashboard.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.rule.view: Seeing any dashboard requires the ViewAnalytics permission.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.rule.conf: Only holders of ConfigureDashboards can build or edit dashboards.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.rule.slug: Each dashboard is opened by its unique, stable slug.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.rule.widg: The widget count reflects only the widgets you are permitted to see.
