analytics.dashboardsList.guide.tip.build: Build a focused custom dashboard per audience rather than one crowded view.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.tip.refre: Refresh after new snapshots run to surface the latest dashboards.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.tip.clust: Use recurrence clusters to spot systemic, repeat-finding themes across audits.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.perm.view: ViewAnalytics — open and read the available dashboards.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.perm.buil: ConfigureDashboards — create, configure and edit dashboards.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.perm.admi: Administrators manage all dashboards and their widgets.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.faq.empty: Why do I see no dashboards?
Either no dashboards are configured yet, or your role lacks the ViewAnalytics permission for the ones that exist.
analytics.dashboardsList.guide.faq.custo: How do I build a custom dashboard?
With the ConfigureDashboards permission, open a dashboard and add widgets to compose the metrics you want to track.
coverage.guide.purpose: See which auditable entities have been covered by audits and where the coverage gaps are.
coverage.guide.description: Coverage Analytics reconciles the audit universe against completed engagements — surfacing entities not audited recently, high-risk blind spots, and a coverage matrix to guide the next audit plan.
coverage.guide.action.notAudited: List entities not audited within a chosen number of months
coverage.guide.action.highRisk: Find high-residual-risk entities that are overdue for audit
coverage.guide.action.matrix: Build a coverage matrix by entity type and audit window
coverage.guide.action.filter: Filter each report by look-back period, entity type or window
coverage.guide.section.notAudited.title: Not-audited-since report
coverage.guide.section.notAudited.body: Lists auditable entities with no completed audit within the chosen months — the core coverage-gap view. "Never" means the entity has never been audited.
coverage.guide.section.highRisk.title: High-risk gaps
coverage.guide.section.highRisk.body: Combines the coverage gap with the entity's composite residual risk, so you can prioritise the riskiest blind spots first.
coverage.guide.section.matrix.title: Coverage matrix
coverage.guide.section.matrix.body: A grid counting audits per entity type across a window; zero cells highlight parts of the universe left uncovered.
coverage.guide.rule.completed: Only completed audits count as coverage — draft or in-progress engagements do not close a gap.
coverage.guide.rule.residual: High-risk gaps are ranked by composite residual score; entities without a score show a dash.
coverage.guide.rule.window: The matrix window is a free-text period (e.g. a year); leave it blank to count all audits.
coverage.guide.tip.highRisk: Run the high-risk report first — it points to the gaps that matter most for the plan.
coverage.guide.tip.window: Set the same window across reports to keep coverage figures comparable year-on-year.
coverage.guide.tip.entityType: Filter by entity type to review coverage for one part of the universe at a time.
coverage.guide.faq.never.q: What does "Never" mean in the last-audited column?
coverage.guide.faq.never.a: The entity has no completed audit on record, so it has never been covered — usually a top priority for the plan.
coverage.guide.faq.residual.q: Why do some high-risk rows show a dash for residual score?
coverage.guide.faq.residual.a: That entity has no composite residual score yet; add risk data in the audit universe to rank it.
ac.packList.guide.purpose: Generate, review and distribute the quarterly Audit Committee report packs presented to the board.
ac.packList.guide.description: This page lists every Audit Committee pack — a point-in-time compilation of findings, analytics and the Chief Internal Auditor's narrative for a reporting period. Generate a new pack for a period, track its status as it builds, and open each version to review, approve and distribute it to committee recipients.
ac.packList.guide.action.generate: Generate a new pack for a reporting period, optionally including a DOCX artefact and a committee-meeting label.
ac.packList.guide.action.filter: Filter the list by pack status to focus on pending, in-review, approved or distributed packs.
ac.packList.guide.action.open: Open a pack version to review its contents, edit the CIA narrative, approve and distribute it.
ac.packList.guide.action.verify: Copy or hover a pack's SHA-256 hash to verify the integrity of the produced artefact.
ac.packList.guide.section.generate.title: Generate a pack
ac.packList.guide.section.generate.body: Requests a new pack for a chosen period; generation runs asynchronously and the button is disabled while it builds.
ac.packList.guide.section.filter.title: Status filter
ac.packList.guide.section.filter.body: Narrows the table to packs in a single lifecycle state — pending, generating, pending review, approved, distributed or failed.
ac.packList.guide.section.table.title: Pack versions
ac.packList.guide.section.table.body: Each row is a versioned pack showing its period, committee meeting, status, content hash and request time; open the version link to act on it.
ac.packList.guide.flow.generate: Request a pack for a reporting period
ac.packList.guide.flow.build: The system compiles findings, analytics and narrative asynchronously
ac.packList.guide.flow.review: CIA reviews and edits the supplementary narrative
ac.packList.guide.flow.approve: CIA approves the pack, locking its content
ac.packList.guide.flow.distribute: Approved pack is distributed to Audit Committee recipients
ac.packList.guide.dep.findings: Findings — the audit findings compiled into the pack, with restricted-visibility filters applied.
ac.packList.guide.dep.reports: Reporting — report content and formats reused to render the pack artefact.
ac.packList.guide.dep.analytics: Analytics — the KPI and trend snapshots embedded in each pack.
ac.packList.guide.dep.identity: Identity — the CIA and committee roles that authorise generation, approval and delivery.
ac.packList.guide.use.detail: Pack detail — opens the selected version to review, approve and download it.
ac.packList.guide.use.distribution: Distribution log — records each delivery of a distributed pack to recipients.
ac.packList.guide.use.dashboard: AC dashboard — the live committee aggregates that reference distributed packs.
ac.packList.guide.use.actions: AC action items — follow-ups raised by the committee from a distributed pack.
ac.packList.guide.rule.async: Pack generation is asynchronous — the list polls until the status settles on approved, distributed or failed.
ac.packList.guide.rule.immutable: A produced pack is content-hashed (SHA-256) and immutable once approved, guaranteeing what the board received.
ac.packList.guide.rule.lifecycle: A pack moves pending → generating → pending review → approved → distributed, and cannot skip states.
ac.packList.guide.rule.restrict: Findings under a visibility restriction are excluded from the pack according to the requester's clearance.
ac.packList.guide.tip.poll: After generating, leave the page open — it polls automatically and notifies you when the pack is ready to review.
ac.packList.guide.tip.hash: Hover the hash column to see the full SHA-256 and confirm a downloaded artefact matches the record.
ac.packList.guide.tip.filter: Use the status filter to quickly separate packs awaiting review from those already distributed.
ac.packList.guide.perm.generate: Generate AC Pack — start a new pack for a reporting period.
ac.packList.guide.perm.cia: Chief Internal Auditor — edit the narrative, approve and distribute packs.
ac.packList.guide.perm.view: View AC Packs — browse the pack list and open versions read-only.
ac.packList.guide.faq.status.q: Why does a new pack stay in 'generating' for a while?
ac.packList.guide.faq.status.a: Generation runs in the background while findings, analytics and the narrative are compiled; the page polls and updates the status automatically.
ac.packList.guide.faq.distribute.q: How does a pack reach the Audit Committee?
ac.packList.guide.faq.distribute.a: Once the CIA approves a pack, distributing it sends the artefact to the committee recipients and logs each delivery in the pack's distribution history.
ac.actionItems.guide.purpose: Track audit-committee directives from a single register through to closure and chair sign-off.
ac.actionItems.guide.description: This workspace holds the action items raised by the audit committee — directives assigned to owners, worked through management, and formally acknowledged by the chair once resolved.
ac.actionItems.guide.action.create: Raise a new committee action item and assign an owner
ac.actionItems.guide.action.progress: Mark an item in progress or record its closure response
ac.actionItems.guide.action.acknowledge: Acknowledge a closed item as committee chair
ac.actionItems.guide.section.create.body: Committee members create a directive here, assign an owner and set a due date. Needs the AC member permission.
ac.actionItems.guide.section.filter.body: Narrow the register to open, in-progress, closed or acknowledged items; the filter re-queries the server.
ac.actionItems.guide.section.table.title: The action register
ac.actionItems.guide.section.table.body: Every directive with its status, assignee and due date, plus the actions to progress, close or acknowledge it.
ac.actionItems.guide.rule.lifecycle: An item moves Open → In progress → Closed → Acknowledged; each step needs the right role.
ac.actionItems.guide.rule.closure: Closing an item requires a closure response describing how it was resolved.
ac.actionItems.guide.rule.acknowledge: Only a closed item can be acknowledged, and only by the committee chair.
ac.actionItems.guide.rule.roles: Members raise items, the CIA progresses and closes them, and the chair acknowledges closure.
ac.actionItems.guide.tip.due: Set a due date when raising an item so owners know the committee's deadline.
ac.actionItems.guide.tip.filter: Filter to open or in-progress items to focus on what still needs the committee's attention.
ac.actionItems.guide.faq.actions.q: Why can't I see the start or close buttons?
ac.actionItems.guide.faq.actions.a: Progressing and closing items is reserved for the Chief Internal Auditor; members can only raise items and the chair only acknowledges closure.
ac.actionItems.guide.faq.acknowledge.q: What does acknowledging an item do?
ac.actionItems.guide.faq.acknowledge.a: It records the committee chair's formal sign-off that a closed item is accepted, completing its lifecycle.
ac.packViewer.guide.purpose: Review a generated audit-committee pack, then approve and distribute it to committee members.
ac.packViewer.guide.description: This page opens a single versioned committee pack — its metadata, downloadable artefacts, CIA narrative, an analytics snapshot, and the full distribution log. The Chief Internal Auditor reviews the pack, adds supplementary commentary, approves the version to seal it, and dispatches it to every audit-committee recipient.
ac.packViewer.guide.action.download: Download the pack in any produced format (PDF and others) from the overview card.
ac.packViewer.guide.action.narrative: Add or edit the CIA supplementary narrative while the pack is pending review.
ac.packViewer.guide.action.approve: Approve the pack to seal this version for committee distribution.
ac.packViewer.guide.action.distribute: Distribute the approved pack to all audit-committee recipients.
ac.packViewer.guide.section.actions.body: CIA-only buttons to edit the narrative, approve the version, and distribute the pack; each appears only at the matching status.
ac.packViewer.guide.section.overview.bod: Version, status, reporting period, SHA-256 integrity hash, and request/approval timestamps, plus download buttons for each artefact format.
ac.packViewer.guide.section.analytics.bo: The plan-completion, exception, sanctions, and recurrence figures captured for this pack version at generation time.
ac.packViewer.guide.section.distribution: An audit trail of every recipient, the pack version they received, when it was dispatched, and the delivery outcome.
ac.packViewer.guide.flow.generate: A committee pack is generated from audit exceptions, sanctions, and analytics
ac.packViewer.guide.flow.review: The CIA reviews the pack and adds a supplementary narrative
ac.packViewer.guide.flow.approve: The CIA approves the version, sealing its content and hash
ac.packViewer.guide.flow.distribute: The approved pack is dispatched to audit-committee recipients
ac.packViewer.guide.flow.comment: Committee members read the pack and post comments
ac.packViewer.guide.dep.exceptions: Audit findings and exceptions that populate the pack narrative
ac.packViewer.guide.dep.sanctions: Sanctions cases feeding the committee analytics
ac.packViewer.guide.dep.analytics: The analytics snapshot compiled at pack generation
ac.packViewer.guide.use.committee: Audit-committee members who receive and read the pack
ac.packViewer.guide.use.distribution: The distribution log that records every dispatch and outcome
ac.packViewer.guide.use.comments: Committee comments captured against this pack for the governance record
ac.packViewer.guide.rule.editState: The CIA narrative can only be edited while the pack is pending review.
ac.packViewer.guide.rule.approveState: A pack can only be approved from pending review, which seals the version.
ac.packViewer.guide.rule.distributeState: Only an approved pack can be distributed to the committee.
ac.packViewer.guide.rule.hash: The SHA-256 hash fingerprints the sealed content so any alteration is detectable.
ac.packViewer.guide.tip.narrative: Write the CIA narrative before approving — it is locked once the version is sealed.
ac.packViewer.guide.tip.hash: Hover the hash to copy the full SHA-256 value when verifying a downloaded pack.
ac.packViewer.guide.tip.log: Check the distribution log to confirm every recipient received the correct version.
ac.packViewer.guide.perm.cia: The Chief Internal Auditor (CIA) can edit the narrative, approve, and distribute.
ac.packViewer.guide.perm.viewer: Other authorised users can view the pack, analytics, and distribution log.
ac.packViewer.guide.faq.disabled.q: Why are the approve and distribute buttons hidden?
ac.packViewer.guide.faq.disabled.a: They appear only for CIA users and only at the matching status — approve at pending review, distribute once approved.
ac.packViewer.guide.faq.hash.q: What is the SHA-256 hash for?
ac.packViewer.guide.faq.hash.a: It is an integrity fingerprint of the sealed pack, so recipients can verify a downloaded copy has not been altered.
sanctions.dcQueue.guide.purpose: Review sanctions cases referred to the Disciplinary Committee and reach a decision.
sanctions.dcQueue.guide.description: This is the Disciplinary Committee's worklist — cases escalated after an HR recommendation land here so committee members can weigh severity, recurrence and context before deciding an outcome.
sanctions.dcQueue.guide.action.review: Review the queue of cases referred for a committee decision
sanctions.dcQueue.guide.action.open: Open a case to see its full evidence and history
sanctions.dcQueue.guide.action.decide: Weigh severity, category and recurrence before deciding
sanctions.dcQueue.guide.action.page: Page through the queue when many cases are pending
sanctions.dcQueue.guide.section.queue.bo: Every case awaiting a committee decision, with its severity, category and trigger date. Click a row to open the case.
The employee under review — shown masked until you open the case, keeping disciplinary matters confidential.
sanctions.dcQueue.guide.section.severity: The proposed severity band carried over from the recommendation, so the committee can triage the most serious cases first.
sanctions.dcQueue.guide.rule.referred: Only cases explicitly referred to the committee appear here — not the whole sanctions register.
sanctions.dcQueue.guide.rule.masked: Subject identity stays masked in the list to protect confidentiality until a case is opened.
sanctions.dcQueue.guide.rule.recurrence: A repeat-offence flag escalates severity per the disciplinary grid and is highlighted on the case.
sanctions.dcQueue.guide.rule.member: Only Disciplinary Committee members can view this queue and record a decision.
sanctions.dcQueue.guide.tip.severity: Work the highest-severity cases first — the severity badge lets you triage at a glance.
sanctions.dcQueue.guide.tip.recurrence: The repeat icon marks recurrence; treat those cases with extra scrutiny.
sanctions.dcQueue.guide.faq.here.q: Why is a case in this queue?
sanctions.dcQueue.guide.faq.here.a: It was referred to the Disciplinary Committee after an HR recommendation and is awaiting a committee decision.
sanctions.dcQueue.guide.faq.masked.q: Why is the employee name hidden?
sanctions.dcQueue.guide.faq.masked.a: Subject identity is masked in the list for confidentiality; open the case to see the full details you are authorised to view.
sanctions.grid.guide.purpose: Define the disciplinary matrix that maps each finding's category and severity to a recommended sanction.
sanctions.grid.guide.description: This is where administrators configure the sanctions grid — each cell pairs a category and severity (plus an optional recurrence flag) with a recommended sanction range the platform suggests when a finding is triaged.
sanctions.grid.guide.action.add: Add a category × severity cell to the matrix
sanctions.grid.guide.action.range: Set the recommended sanction range for each cell
sanctions.grid.guide.action.save: Save your changes as a new draft version
sanctions.grid.guide.action.activate: Activate a version as the live grid
sanctions.grid.guide.section.matrix.body: Each row is a category × severity cell with its recommended sanction range; edit a range inline or remove a cell.
sanctions.grid.guide.section.add.title: Add a cell
sanctions.grid.guide.section.add.body: Pick a category and severity — flag recurrence for repeat offences — to add a new cell to the matrix.
sanctions.grid.guide.section.actions.bod: Save your edits as a new draft version, then activate it to replace the live grid. Both steps may need a second approver.
sanctions.grid.guide.rule.version: Each save creates a new version; only one grid is active at a time.
sanctions.grid.guide.rule.makerchecker: Saving and activating are maker-checker gated — a second approver may be required before changes take effect.
sanctions.grid.guide.rule.key: Each cell is unique by category, severity and recurrence flag.
sanctions.grid.guide.rule.reason: Activating a version requires a justification of at least 20 characters.
sanctions.grid.guide.tip.recurrence: Add a separate recurrence cell to escalate repeat offences.
sanctions.grid.guide.tip.range: Use a range (e.g. 'Written warning to suspension') to give approvers discretion.
sanctions.grid.guide.tip.activate: Save and review a draft before activating it as the live grid.
sanctions.grid.guide.faq.pending.q: Why was my save marked pending?
sanctions.grid.guide.faq.pending.a: Grid changes are maker-checker gated; a second approver must confirm before they take effect.
sanctions.grid.guide.faq.active.q: How do I make a grid live?
sanctions.grid.guide.faq.active.a: Save your changes, then activate the version with a reason — it replaces the current active grid.
config.list.guide.purpose: Manage the organization's versioned system-configuration domains and their change history from one place.
config.list.guide.description: This is the admin landing page for configurable domains such as exception defaults and SLAs. Each domain keeps a versioned history with one active version, and settings here drive how findings, recurrence, analytics and reports behave across AuditX.
config.list.guide.action.browse: Browse the available configuration domains shown as cards.
config.list.guide.action.open: Open a domain to view its active version, history and draft editor.
config.list.guide.action.version: Create, activate or roll back configuration versions inside a domain.
config.list.guide.section.grid.title: Configuration domains
config.list.guide.section.grid.body: Each card is an independently versioned configuration domain you can open and edit; more domains appear here as they are added.
config.list.guide.section.card.title: Domain card
config.list.guide.section.card.body: Click a card to open the domain's detail page, where you review the active version, browse history and submit a typed draft.
config.list.guide.section.code.title: Domain code
config.list.guide.section.code.body: The stable machine key (e.g. exception_defaults) used by the API and in version history to identify this domain.
config.list.guide.dep.identity: Identity & access — your role determines whether you can view or manage configuration.
config.list.guide.dep.makerChecker: Maker-checker — sensitive activations and rollbacks may be gated for approval before taking effect.
config.list.guide.dep.reference: Reference data — domains define the defaults other modules read at runtime.
config.list.guide.use.findings: Findings — exception defaults set target remediation days per severity and recurrence detection.
config.list.guide.use.analytics: Analytics — SLA and recurrence thresholds feed overdue and repeat-issue metrics.
config.list.guide.use.reports: Reports — configured thresholds shape the numbers surfaced in generated reports.
config.list.guide.rule.versioned: Each domain is versioned with at most one active version plus a history of prior drafts.
config.list.guide.rule.reason: Every configuration change requires a change reason for the audit trail.
config.list.guide.rule.gated: Activations and rollbacks can be routed through maker-checker approval before they apply.
config.list.guide.rule.rollback: You can roll back to any previous version, which itself creates a new tracked change.
config.list.guide.tip.reason: Write a clear change reason — it becomes the permanent record of why the setting changed.
config.list.guide.tip.rollback: If a change causes problems, roll back to the last known-good version rather than editing under pressure.
config.list.guide.perm.view: View configuration — read domains, active versions and history.
config.list.guide.perm.manage: Manage configuration — create drafts and activate or roll back versions.
config.list.guide.faq.domains.a: A domain is a self-contained, versioned group of settings — such as exception defaults and SLAs — that other AuditX modules read at runtime.
config.list.guide.faq.activate.q: How does a new setting take effect?
config.list.guide.faq.activate.a: Open the domain, edit a typed draft with a change reason, then activate it; once active (after any maker-checker approval) it applies platform-wide.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.purpose: Detect tampered audit evidence by re-verifying uploaded files against the SHA-256 hash captured at upload.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.description: This console lists every evidence file whose current contents no longer match the cryptographic hash recorded when it was first attached to an audit — the primary signal that a stored artefact was altered, corrupted, or replaced. Administrators review each flagged file, confirm whether the mismatch is a genuine integrity breach or an expected re-upload, and clear the flag with a documented resolution once handled.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.action.review: Review the list of evidence files flagged for a hash mismatch.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.action.inspect: Inspect each file's name, owning audit, stored SHA-256 hash, and upload time.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.action.unflag: Clear a flag by recording a resolution once the mismatch is investigated.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.action.retry: Retry loading the flagged-evidence list if the request fails.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.section.table.bo: Each row is an evidence file whose live contents diverge from its stored hash, showing the filename, owning audit, hash, and upload timestamp.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.section.hash.bod: The cryptographic fingerprint captured at upload; the file was flagged because re-hashing its current bytes no longer produces this value.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.section.unflag.b: Once you have investigated the mismatch, clear the flag and record a resolution note that is written to the audit trail.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.flow.upload: An auditor uploads an evidence file against an audit.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.flow.hash: The system computes and stores the file's SHA-256 hash.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.flow.reverify: A later integrity check re-hashes the stored bytes.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.flow.flag: A hash mismatch flags the file and surfaces it here.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.flow.resolve: An administrator investigates and clears the flag with a resolution.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.dep.audits: Audits — the engagement each flagged file belongs to.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.dep.evidence: Evidence attachments captured during audit execution.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.dep.trail: Audit trail — records the original upload hash and every unflag action.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.use.findings: Findings — supporting evidence whose integrity underpins a finding.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.use.reports: Reports — assurance that cited evidence is untampered.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.use.trail: Audit trail — resolution notes are appended when a flag is cleared.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.rule.hashMatch: A file is flagged whenever its current hash differs from the hash stored at upload.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.rule.immutable: Evidence files are meant to be immutable once attached, so any hash change is treated as suspicious.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.rule.resolution: Clearing a flag requires a resolution note, which is persisted for accountability.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.rule.tenant: Only flagged evidence within your own tenant is listed and actionable.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.tip.empty: An empty list is the healthy state — it means no stored evidence has failed its integrity check.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.tip.reupload: If a mismatch stems from a legitimate re-upload, note that in the resolution rather than deleting the file.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.perm.admin: Administrators with admin-operations access can view and clear integrity flags.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.perm.auditor: Auditors upload the evidence whose hashes are monitored here but do not resolve flags.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.faq.why.q: Why does a file appear on this page?
evidenceIntegrity.guide.faq.why.a: Its contents were re-hashed and no longer match the SHA-256 fingerprint recorded when it was first uploaded, indicating possible tampering or corruption.
evidenceIntegrity.guide.faq.unflag.q: What happens when I unflag a file?
evidenceIntegrity.guide.faq.unflag.a: The flag is cleared with your resolution note and the file drops off this list; the action is recorded in the audit trail for accountability.
identity.makerChecker.guide.purpose: Apply dual control to sensitive identity changes — a second authoriser must approve before they take effect.
identity.makerChecker.guide.description: This is the maker-checker (four-eyes) queue: role and access changes raised by one administrator wait here for a different authoriser to approve or reject, giving the identity module a segregation-of-duties safeguard.
identity.makerChecker.guide.action.filte: Filter the queue by action type to focus your review
identity.makerChecker.guide.action.appro: Approve a pending change, which applies it immediately
identity.makerChecker.guide.action.rejec: Reject a change with a recorded reason
identity.makerChecker.guide.action.refre: Refresh to pull the latest pending actions
identity.makerChecker.guide.section.filt: Narrow the queue to role creates, updates, archives or user role grants so you only see the changes you want to review.
identity.makerChecker.guide.section.tabl: Each row shows the action, its target object, the administrator who raised it and when — the context you need to make a decision.
identity.makerChecker.guide.section.deci: Approve applies the change instantly; Reject prompts for a reason. You cannot action a change you raised yourself.
identity.makerChecker.guide.rule.selfApp: You cannot approve or reject a change you raised — a different authoriser must action it.
identity.makerChecker.guide.rule.immedia: Approving a change applies it immediately across the identity module.
identity.makerChecker.guide.rule.reason: Rejecting a change requires a reason, which is recorded in the audit trail.
identity.makerChecker.guide.rule.scope: Only sensitive actions — role create, update, archive and user role grants — are routed through maker-checker.
identity.makerChecker.guide.tip.filter: Filter by action type when the queue is long to review one category at a time.
identity.makerChecker.guide.tip.verify: Check the target and the raising administrator before approving a change.
identity.makerChecker.guide.perm.maker: The administrator who raised the change (cannot self-approve)
identity.makerChecker.guide.faq.self.q: Why can't I approve this change?
identity.makerChecker.guide.faq.self.a: Dual control blocks self-approval — a change you raised must be approved by a different authoriser.
What happens when I approve a change?
It is applied immediately — the role or user role grant takes effect and the decision is recorded in the audit trail.
administration.bankSettings.guide.purpos: Configure your organization's identity, branding, governance rules and resource limits in one place.
administration.bankSettings.guide.descri: This page holds the organization-wide settings that shape the whole platform: the display name, timezone and default locale, the brand colors and logo/icon applied across the app, governance toggles for planning and audit launch, and the evidence file/storage limits. Changes take effect immediately for every user.
administration.bankSettings.guide.action: Set the organization display name, timezone and default locale.
Choose brand colors and upload the logo and app icon.
Toggle governance rules for plan overlap and pre-approval audit launch.
Set the maximum evidence file size and per-audit storage cap.
administration.bankSettings.guide.sectio: Name your organization and set the timezone, default locale and optional Active Directory provisioning filters (OU DN and group SID) used when syncing users.
Pick primary and accent colors and upload a logo and icon (image files up to 512 KB); saving re-themes the running app in place so you see the change without reloading.
Cap the maximum size of a single evidence file (MB) and total evidence storage per audit (GB); these guard rails apply to every audit's evidence uploads.
administration.bankSettings.guide.dep.pe: Manage organization settings / configure limits permissions, which gate who can edit here.
administration.bankSettings.guide.dep.di: Active Directory, when provisioning filters are used to sync users and groups.
administration.bankSettings.guide.use.br: The app shell, login screen and reports, which render the organization name, colors and logo.
administration.bankSettings.guide.use.pl: Annual planning and audit launch, which honor the plan-overlap and pre-approval rules.
administration.bankSettings.guide.use.ev: Evidence uploads across all audits, which enforce the file-size and storage limits.
administration.bankSettings.guide.rule.c: Primary and accent colors must be valid 6-digit hex values (e.g. #4f46e5).
administration.bankSettings.guide.rule.a: Logo and icon uploads must be image files no larger than 512 KB.
administration.bankSettings.guide.rule.o: With plan overlap off, a plan covering a period that overlaps an existing plan is rejected; with pre-approval launch off, audits can only launch from an approved plan.
administration.bankSettings.guide.rule.l: Evidence file and per-audit storage limits must each be at least 1.
administration.bankSettings.guide.tip.pr: Save settings to instantly re-theme the app — the new colors, name and logo apply without a page reload.
administration.bankSettings.guide.tip.lo: Set the default locale (e.g. en-GB) to control how new users see dates, numbers and language until they choose their own.
administration.bankSettings.guide.perm.m: Manage organization settings — edit identity, branding and governance rules.
administration.bankSettings.guide.perm.l: Configure limits — edit the evidence file and storage limits.
administration.bankSettings.guide.faq.ap: Do branding changes require users to reload?
No — saving applies the new name, colors and logo to the running app immediately, and other users pick them up on their next load.
administration.bankSettings.guide.faq.li: Why are resource limits saved separately?
They are governed by a distinct Configure limits permission and saved on their own so administrators without that right can still manage the other settings.
administration.systemHealth.guide.purpos: Give administrators a point-in-time snapshot of the platform's overall status and key operating counts.
administration.systemHealth.guide.descri: System Health surfaces an overall status indicator plus live tallies of active users, total users, audit templates, and configured integrations, so administrators can confirm the platform is running normally and spot problems early.
administration.systemHealth.guide.action: Read the overall status badge and the timestamp of the current health snapshot.
Review the key platform counts — active users, total users, templates, and integrations.
Retry the health check to fetch a fresh snapshot if it fails to load.
administration.systemHealth.guide.sectio: The status badge summarises platform health and shows when this snapshot was generated.
Cards report active users, total users, audit templates, and configured integrations at a glance.
administration.systemHealth.guide.flow.c: The organization, users, templates, and integrations are configured in Administration.
administration.systemHealth.guide.flow.o: Accounts, templates, and integrations accumulate as teams use the platform.
administration.systemHealth.guide.flow.s: The API aggregates a health snapshot on request.
administration.systemHealth.guide.flow.r: Administrators open this page to review status and counts.
administration.systemHealth.guide.dep.us: User accounts — supply the active and total user counts.
administration.systemHealth.guide.dep.te: Audit templates — supply the template count.
administration.systemHealth.guide.dep.in: External integrations — supply the integration count.
administration.systemHealth.guide.dep.ap: The /admin/system-health endpoint that aggregates the snapshot.
administration.systemHealth.guide.use.ad: The Administration console, as its monitoring surface.
administration.systemHealth.guide.use.su: Support and operations teams triaging platform issues.
administration.systemHealth.guide.use.re: Release and backup checks confirming the system is ready.
administration.systemHealth.guide.rule.p: Access requires the View System Health permission.
administration.systemHealth.guide.rule.r: This page is read-only — it reports state and never changes it.
administration.systemHealth.guide.rule.s: Counts reflect a point-in-time snapshot taken at the generated timestamp.
administration.systemHealth.guide.rule.a: The active-user count includes only enabled, non-locked accounts.
administration.systemHealth.guide.tip.re: If the snapshot fails to load, use retry before assuming an outage.
administration.systemHealth.guide.tip.de: When the status is not healthy, check integrations first — they are the most common cause.
administration.systemHealth.guide.perm.a: System administrators granted View System Health.
administration.systemHealth.guide.perm.o: Support and operations roles granted the health permission.
administration.systemHealth.guide.faq.st: What does the status badge mean?
It summarises the platform's overall health as reported by the server at the snapshot time; anything other than healthy warrants investigation.
administration.systemHealth.guide.faq.fr: They are a point-in-time snapshot regenerated each time the page loads or you retry — the timestamp shows exactly when.
administration.releases.guide.purpose: Install and verify signed product releases, and keep an auditable record of every update.
administration.releases.guide.descriptio: This is the update-management console — submit a signed release, let the platform verify its signature and manifest hash before it is applied, and review the full history of install attempts.
administration.releases.guide.action.ins: Submit a signed release to verify and install
administration.releases.guide.action.cha: Cite the change-record reference that authorises the update
administration.releases.guide.action.rev: Review the history of installs, verifications and rejections
administration.releases.guide.action.ret: Re-submit with corrected values when a release is rejected
administration.releases.guide.section.fo: Enter the version, change-record reference, manifest SHA-256, and the base64 signature and manifest content produced by your build pipeline.
administration.releases.guide.section.ve: The platform checks the signature and manifest hash before applying the release; only a valid package is installed, and the result is recorded.
administration.releases.guide.section.hi: Every attempt is logged with its version, status, change record and detail — an immutable trail for change management.
administration.releases.guide.rule.verif: A release is applied only if its signature and manifest hash verify; otherwise it is Rejected.
administration.releases.guide.rule.chang: Every install must cite a change-record reference to satisfy change-management controls.
administration.releases.guide.rule.immut: Install attempts — including rejections — are permanent log records and are never deleted.
administration.releases.guide.tip.hash: Paste the exact manifest SHA-256 emitted by your build pipeline to avoid a hash-mismatch rejection.
administration.releases.guide.tip.reject: A rejected release stays in the history as evidence — fix the values and submit again.
administration.releases.guide.faq.reject: The signature or the manifest hash did not verify; check the SHA-256, signature and manifest content and re-submit.
administration.releases.guide.faq.change: Why do I need a change-record reference?
It ties each update to an approved change, providing the audit evidence required by change-management controls.
administration.support.guide.purpose: Grant vendor support engineers time-boxed, break-glass access to assist with an incident.
administration.support.guide.description: The support channel lets an administrator open a temporary, auto-expiring access window for named external support engineers, review whether that access is currently active, and revoke it the moment it is no longer needed.
administration.support.guide.action.stat: Review whether vendor support access is currently active, who holds it, and when it expires.
administration.support.guide.action.gran: Name the support engineers who may connect during the assistance window.
administration.support.guide.action.dura: Set how many minutes the access window stays open before it auto-expires.
administration.support.guide.action.revo: Immediately cut off active vendor access before its scheduled expiry.
administration.support.guide.section.sta: Shows the active/inactive badge, the granted engineers, the enabled time, and the expiry, with a Revoke button while access is live.
administration.support.guide.section.eng: Add one chip per external engineer identifier (their email) who should be allowed in during this window.
administration.support.guide.section.gra: Enter a duration in minutes and enable the window; access opens for the listed engineers and expires automatically when the timer ends.
administration.support.guide.flow.reques: Vendor requests access to investigate an incident
administration.support.guide.flow.grant: Administrator lists engineers and enables a timed window
administration.support.guide.flow.assist: Support engineers connect and assist during the window
administration.support.guide.flow.expire: Window auto-expires or is revoked, closing access
administration.support.guide.dep.permiss: Requires the Manage Support Channel permission to view or change access.
administration.support.guide.dep.identit: Engineer identifiers map to external accounts recognised by identity and access control.
administration.support.guide.use.audit: Every grant and revoke is written to the audit trail for accountability.
administration.support.guide.use.health: Support engineers use their window to diagnose issues surfaced in System Health.
administration.support.guide.rule.durati: Duration must be between 1 and 1440 minutes (up to 24 hours).
administration.support.guide.rule.expiry: Access closes automatically once the window expires — no manual step required.
administration.support.guide.rule.revoke: Revoking access takes effect immediately and asks for confirmation first.
administration.support.guide.rule.identi: At least one engineer identifier is required before a window can be enabled.
administration.support.guide.tip.shortes: Grant the shortest window that still lets the engineer finish the task.
administration.support.guide.tip.revoke: Revoke as soon as the assistance ends rather than waiting for expiry.
administration.support.guide.perm.manage: Manage Support Channel — enable, view, and revoke vendor access.
What happens when the window expires?
Access is closed automatically at the expiry time; the engineers must be re-granted a new window to continue.
administration.support.guide.faq.who.q: Who can see and manage this page?
administration.support.guide.faq.who.a: Only administrators holding the Manage Support Channel permission can open, view, or revoke a support window.
administration.backup.guide.purpose: Prove that backups are restorable and recover individual records from a point-in-time snapshot under approval.
administration.backup.guide.description: This is the disaster-recovery workbench: log periodic restore-drill results to evidence backup integrity, and raise justified object-restore requests that a second approver reviews before data is rolled back.
administration.backup.guide.action.drill: Record the outcome and details of a backup restore-drill test.
administration.backup.guide.action.reque: Request restore of a specific object from a chosen snapshot date with justification.
administration.backup.guide.action.decid: Approve or reject a pending object-restore request under dual control.
administration.backup.guide.action.histo: Review the chronological log of past restore drills and their outcomes.
administration.backup.guide.section.dril: Log the result (Success or Failed) and details of each backup restore test to evidence recoverability.
administration.backup.guide.section.rest: Identify the object type, ID, snapshot date and justification to request a point-in-time recovery.
administration.backup.guide.section.hist: An append-only record of every restore drill, when it ran and whether it succeeded.
administration.backup.guide.flow.backup: The platform captures automated backup snapshots.
administration.backup.guide.flow.drill: A restore drill is scheduled to test recovery.
administration.backup.guide.flow.record: The drill outcome is recorded here as DR evidence.
administration.backup.guide.flow.request: On data loss, an object restore is requested with justification.
administration.backup.guide.flow.approve: A second approver reviews the request and the object is restored.
administration.backup.guide.dep.backups: Requires backup snapshots retained by the platform's backup pipeline.
administration.backup.guide.dep.retentio: Retention policy determines which snapshot dates are available.
administration.backup.guide.dep.rbac: Requires the retention and restore permissions granted through RBAC.
administration.backup.guide.use.complian: Drill records evidence disaster-recovery readiness for regulators and auditors.
administration.backup.guide.use.auditTra: Restore requests and approval decisions are written to the audit trail.
administration.backup.guide.rule.dualCon: A restore request must be approved by a separate reviewer before it takes effect.
administration.backup.guide.rule.justifi: Every object-restore request requires a justification.
administration.backup.guide.rule.outcome: Each drill must record an outcome (Success or Failed) with details.
administration.backup.guide.rule.immutab: Drill history is append-only and cannot be edited or deleted.
administration.backup.guide.tip.cadence: Run restore drills on a regular cadence to keep DR evidence current.
administration.backup.guide.tip.details: Record specific details such as dataset, duration and issues so drills stay auditable.
administration.backup.guide.tip.snapshot: Choose the snapshot date just before the data was lost to minimise the rollback.
administration.backup.guide.perm.retenti: Manage Retention lets you record restore drills.
administration.backup.guide.perm.restore: Execute Restore lets you request and decide object restores.
administration.backup.guide.perm.separat: The approver should differ from the requester to preserve separation of duties.
administration.backup.guide.faq.drill.a: A test that restores from backup to prove the backups are usable, whose outcome you log here as disaster-recovery evidence.
administration.backup.guide.faq.undo.q: Can I undo an object restore?
administration.backup.guide.faq.undo.a: No — a restore overwrites current data with the snapshot, so review the justification carefully before approving.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.purpose: Provision many user accounts in a single batch instead of creating them one at a time.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.descripti: The import users console lets administrators onboard new people from a CSV file, with a per-row results table showing exactly which records succeeded and which failed and why. To activate or deactivate existing users in bulk, select them in the Users list under Access Control.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.action.im: Import a batch of new users from a CSV file or pasted rows (email, first name, last name, role).
administration.bulkUsers.guide.action.up: Upload a .csv file to populate the import field, or paste the rows directly.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.action.re: Review the results table to see which rows succeeded and which failed with their reasons.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.section.i: Upload or paste CSV rows to provision new user accounts in a single batch.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.section.u: Pick a .csv file from your machine; its contents load into the field so you can review them before importing.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.flow.prep: Prepare a CSV with email, first name, last name and role columns.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.flow.uplo: Upload the file or paste the rows into the import panel.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.flow.prov: Submit to provision the accounts in bulk.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.flow.revi: Review the results table and correct any failed rows.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.flow.onbo: New users receive their sign-in invitation and appear in the directory.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.dep.csv: A correctly formatted CSV source (email, first name, last name, role).
administration.bulkUsers.guide.dep.roles: Roles and permissions — each imported user is assigned a valid role.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.dep.users: User directory — supplies the accounts and IDs this page creates.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.use.users: User management — imported accounts appear in the user directory.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.use.audit: Audit teams — provisioned users can be assigned to audits and tasks.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.use.acces: Access control — imported users gain sign-in and module access per their role.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.rule.form: CSV rows must follow the email, first name, last name, role column order shown in the placeholder.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.rule.dupl: Existing email addresses are reported as errors rather than creating duplicate accounts.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.rule.part: Processing is per-row: valid rows succeed even when others in the batch fail.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.tip.small: Import a small batch first to confirm your CSV format before a large upload.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.tip.error: Use the error table's identifier and message columns to fix and re-run only the failed rows.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.tip.ids: To activate or deactivate accounts in bulk, multi-select users in the Users list under Access Control.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.perm.admi: Administrators can import users in bulk.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.perm.mana: Requires the manage-users permission on the Administration console.
administration.bulkUsers.guide.faq.forma: What columns does the import CSV need?
Email, first name, last name and role, in that order, matching the placeholder header row.
Can I reverse a bulk deactivation?
Yes — reactivate the affected accounts individually from the user management page.
configuration.detail.guide.purpose: Review, edit, and version-control the settings for a single configuration domain.
configuration.detail.guide.description: This page shows the currently active values for a configuration domain, lets authorised users draft a new version, and keeps a full version history with activate and rollback actions. Changes are audited and can be routed to a second approver before they take effect.
configuration.detail.guide.action.review: Review the currently active version's values and when it was activated.
configuration.detail.guide.action.draft: Draft a new version by editing the typed fields and supplying a change reason.
configuration.detail.guide.action.activa: Activate an earlier or newly drafted version to make it the live configuration.
configuration.detail.guide.action.rollba: Roll back to a previous version if a change needs to be reverted.
configuration.detail.guide.section.activ: The settings currently in force for this domain, such as exception target days and recurrence thresholds.
configuration.detail.guide.section.draft: Edit the typed fields and enter a change reason to save a new inactive draft ready for activation.
configuration.detail.guide.section.histo: Every version with its state, change reason, and timestamps; activate or roll back to any earlier version from here.
configuration.detail.guide.flow.apply: New settings apply across the platform
configuration.detail.guide.dep.domains: Configuration domains registry, which lists the available settings groups.
configuration.detail.guide.dep.approvals: The maker-checker approval workflow, which may gate activation and rollback.
configuration.detail.guide.dep.permissio: The Manage Configuration permission, required to draft, activate, or roll back.
configuration.detail.guide.use.exception: Exception management, which reads target days and recurrence rules from these defaults.
configuration.detail.guide.use.analytics: Analytics and KPIs, which apply these thresholds when scoring ageing and recurrence.
configuration.detail.guide.use.reports: Reports, which reflect the active configuration in their calculations.
configuration.detail.guide.rule.single: Only one version is active at a time; activating a version deactivates the previous one.
configuration.detail.guide.rule.reason: Every draft, activation, and rollback requires a change reason of at least 20 characters.
configuration.detail.guide.rule.checker: When maker-checker is enabled, activation and rollback are held pending a second approver before taking effect.
configuration.detail.guide.rule.immutabl: Saved versions are immutable; corrections are made by drafting and activating a new version.
configuration.detail.guide.tip.reason: Write a clear, specific change reason — it becomes the permanent audit trail for the version.
configuration.detail.guide.tip.rollback: Rolling back creates and activates a return to an earlier version rather than deleting later ones.
configuration.detail.guide.tip.refresh: Use Refresh to reload the active version and history after another approver acts.
configuration.detail.guide.perm.manage: Users with Manage Configuration can draft, activate, and roll back versions.
configuration.detail.guide.perm.viewer: Other authorised users can view the active values and version history in read-only mode.
configuration.detail.guide.faq.pending.q: Why does my activation show a pending banner instead of applying?
configuration.detail.guide.faq.pending.a: Maker-checker is enabled for this action, so it was routed to a second approver and takes effect only once they approve it.
What happens when I roll back to a previous version?
The selected earlier version becomes active again; if it is already the active version the action is rejected with a warning.
audits.detail.guide.purpose: Run a single audit engagement end to end — its scope, team, checklist, lifecycle, and findings.
audits.detail.guide.description: This page is the home for one audit. It shows the overview (window, lead, auditee, template, and linked plan item), the audit team, and the checklist organised into sections, plus the lifecycle actions that move the audit from Draft through Planned, In Progress, Under Review, and Completed. Linked exceptions and the activity timeline give you findings and a full audit trail.
audits.detail.guide.action.transition: Move the audit through its lifecycle — plan, launch, send to review, complete, cancel, or reopen — from the header toolbar.
audits.detail.guide.action.team: Add or remove team members and transfer the lead auditor.
audits.detail.guide.action.checklist: Build the checklist — add sections and items, then drag to reorder or move items across sections.
audits.detail.guide.action.fieldwork: Open fieldwork to record responses, or generate reports for the engagement.
audits.detail.guide.section.lifecycle.bo: The header toolbar shows only the transitions valid for the current status — plan, start, send to review, complete, return, reopen, or cancel.
audits.detail.guide.section.overview.bod: Key facts about the engagement: the audit window, lead and auditee, the source template, the linked annual-plan item, and the scope description.
audits.detail.guide.section.team.title: Audit team
audits.detail.guide.section.team.body: The people staffed on this audit and their roles; add or remove auditors and reviewers, or transfer the lead here.
audits.detail.guide.section.checklist.bo: The work programme grouped into sections; add items, reorder by dragging, and see each item's response type and assignee.
audits.detail.guide.flow.create: An audit is created from the audits list, optionally seeded by a template and linked to an annual-plan item.
audits.detail.guide.flow.draft: In Draft you assemble the team and build out the checklist and its sections.
audits.detail.guide.flow.plan: Planning locks the scope; launching the audit starts fieldwork.
audits.detail.guide.flow.execute: During fieldwork auditors respond to each checklist item and raise exceptions.
audits.detail.guide.flow.review: Completed responses are sent for review, then the audit is completed or returned.
audits.detail.guide.dep.template: Checklist templates, which can preload this audit's sections and items.
audits.detail.guide.dep.users: Users, who staff the audit team as lead, auditor, or reviewer.
audits.detail.guide.dep.plan: The annual plan, which supplies the linked plan item this audit fulfils.
audits.detail.guide.dep.refdata: Reference data, which resolves the audit-type code to its label.
audits.detail.guide.use.fieldwork: Fieldwork, where the checklist is answered and evidence is captured.
audits.detail.guide.use.exceptions: Exceptions, the findings raised against this audit.
audits.detail.guide.use.reports: Reports, which summarise the engagement's results.
audits.detail.guide.use.analytics: Analytics, which aggregate audit progress and outcomes across the portfolio.
audits.detail.guide.rule.plan: Planning requires at least one checklist item and at least one assigned auditor.
audits.detail.guide.rule.checklist: Checklist items may be added in Draft or In Progress, but edited or removed only in Draft.
audits.detail.guide.rule.review: Sending to review while items are still unanswered requires a justification reason.
audits.detail.guide.rule.readonly: Completed and cancelled audits are read-only; reopening returns the audit to Draft.
audits.detail.guide.tip.drag: Drag a section's handle to reorder whole sections, or drag items across sections to regroup them.
audits.detail.guide.tip.transfer: Use Transfer Lead to hand off the engagement to another auditor without losing history.
audits.detail.guide.tip.timeline: The activity timeline records every lifecycle, team, and checklist change with who and when.
audits.detail.guide.perm.manage: Manage Audit — assemble the team, edit the checklist, and run lifecycle transitions.
audits.detail.guide.perm.report: View Report — open and generate reports for this audit.
audits.detail.guide.perm.exceptions: View Exceptions — see the findings linked to this audit.
audits.detail.guide.faq.plan.q: Why can't I plan the audit?
audits.detail.guide.faq.plan.a: Planning needs at least one checklist item and one assigned auditor; the Plan button's tooltip lists what is still missing.
audits.detail.guide.faq.findings.a: Open fieldwork to answer checklist items and raise exceptions; those exceptions then appear in the Exceptions section on this page.
exceptions.detail.guide.purpose: Manage a single audit finding from open through remediation to verified closure.
exceptions.detail.guide.description: This page is the workspace for one exception: its overview and root cause, the management action plan with per-action evidence, follow-up verification, closure, and its links to controls and regulations.
exceptions.detail.guide.action.map: Submit, approve or reject the management action plan and mark actions complete.
exceptions.detail.guide.action.evidence: Upload and download remediation evidence against each action.
exceptions.detail.guide.action.close: Close the finding once remediated, or reopen it for follow-up.
exceptions.detail.guide.action.links: Link the finding to affected controls and regulations.
exceptions.detail.guide.section.status.b: Badges here show the finding's current lifecycle status, severity, and flags such as overdue, recurrence, or reopened.
exceptions.detail.guide.section.overview: Target date, owner, who raised it, category, root cause and recommendation, plus a link back to the parent audit.
exceptions.detail.guide.section.map.body: The remediation actions with their owners, due dates and status; work them, attach evidence, and mark them complete here.
exceptions.detail.guide.section.links.bo: The controls and regulatory requirements this finding relates to, kept in sync for compliance reporting.
exceptions.detail.guide.flow.map: Owner submits a management action plan for approval
exceptions.detail.guide.flow.close: Finding closed once remediation is confirmed
exceptions.detail.guide.flow.verify: Follow-up verification checks the fix held
exceptions.detail.guide.dep.audit: Parent audit that raised this finding
exceptions.detail.guide.dep.controls: Controls and regulations available to link
exceptions.detail.guide.rule.lifecycle: The finding moves through a fixed lifecycle: open, MAP submitted/approved, pending closure, closed.
exceptions.detail.guide.rule.mapApproval: A submitted action plan must be approved before actions can be worked and marked complete.
exceptions.detail.guide.rule.evidence: All plan actions must be complete before the finding can move to closure.
exceptions.detail.guide.rule.readonly: Once closed or cancelled the finding is read-only until it is reopened.
exceptions.detail.guide.tip.rootCause: Record a clear root cause and recommendation so remediation targets the real problem.
exceptions.detail.guide.tip.history: Use the History action to see every status change and who made it.
exceptions.detail.guide.tip.reopen: Reopen a closed finding if verification fails or the issue recurs.
exceptions.detail.guide.perm.owner: Owners submit the action plan, upload evidence and mark actions complete.
exceptions.detail.guide.perm.approver: Approvers review, approve or reject the plan and close the finding.
exceptions.detail.guide.perm.cia: The CIA countersigns closures that require sign-off.
exceptions.detail.guide.faq.close.q: Why can't I close this finding yet?
exceptions.detail.guide.faq.close.a: Closure needs an approved action plan with every action marked complete, and the finding in the pending-closure state.
exceptions.detail.guide.faq.reject.q: What happens when a management action plan is rejected?
exceptions.detail.guide.faq.reject.a: The finding returns to a rejected state with the reason recorded, and the owner can revise and resubmit the plan.
planning.detail.guide.purpose: Manage one annual audit plan — its items, approval workflow, coverage and the audits launched from it.
planning.detail.guide.description: This is the working view of a single annual plan. Build the item list, move the plan through submission and approval, then launch audit engagements from approved items and watch execution progress roll up.
planning.detail.guide.action.items: Add, reorder and remove plan items while the plan is editable
planning.detail.guide.action.workflow: Move the plan through its lifecycle — submit, request revision, decide and close
planning.detail.guide.action.launch: Launch an audit engagement from an approved plan item
planning.detail.guide.action.track: Track coverage and checklist execution progress across the plan
planning.detail.guide.section.actions.bo: The toolbar for the plan's lifecycle — submit for approval, submit a revision, record a decision or close. Which buttons appear depends on the current status and your role.
planning.detail.guide.section.status.bod: The current lifecycle badge plus submitted, approved and decision timestamps so you can see where the plan stands at a glance.
Live roll-up of item completion and checklist progress across every launched audit, plus a warning list of items running behind schedule.
planning.detail.guide.section.timeline.b: A Gantt view of every plan item across the plan period — each bar is an engagement's planned window, coloured by status, with a marker for today. Spot overlaps, clustering and gaps at a glance.
planning.detail.guide.section.items.body: Every planned engagement with its window, effort, lead and status. Drag to reorder while editable, and launch an audit from an approved item.
planning.detail.guide.rule.editable: Items can be added, reordered or removed only while the plan is a draft or has revisions requested.
planning.detail.guide.rule.approval: Only the Audit Committee Chair can approve, reject or request revisions on a submitted plan.
planning.detail.guide.rule.launch: Audits can be launched only once the plan is in a linkable state (typically approved); each item links to one audit.
planning.detail.guide.rule.revision: An approved plan can be revised — resubmit changes for a fresh committee decision rather than editing in place.
planning.detail.guide.tip.reorder: Drag the handle to reorder items; the new sequence saves automatically while the plan is editable.
planning.detail.guide.tip.effort: Set an estimated effort per item to make workload and resourcing visible before launch.
planning.detail.guide.tip.behind: Watch the behind-schedule list — it flags launched audits past their planned end date.
planning.detail.guide.faq.launch.q: Why is the Launch audit button disabled?
planning.detail.guide.faq.launch.a: The plan must be in an approved, linkable state and you need the Create audit permission; until then the button stays visible but disabled.
planning.detail.guide.faq.revision.q: How do I change an already-approved plan?
planning.detail.guide.faq.revision.a: Use Submit revision to send updated items back to the Audit Committee for a new decision — the approved baseline stays intact until they decide.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.purpose: Manage the full disciplinary lifecycle of a single sanctions case, from recommendation through decision, appeal and closure.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.description: This page consolidates one disciplinary case: the masked subject, the linked exception that triggered it, the recommendation weighed against the sanctions grid, the HR outcome or Disciplinary Committee decision, any appeal, and closure. Available actions change with the case status, mirroring the backend state machine.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.action.recomm: Draft, edit and submit the recommended sanction against the grid range.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.action.outcom: Record the HR outcome, refer the case to the Disciplinary Committee, or capture its decision.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.action.appeal: File an appeal and record the appeal authority's decision.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.action.dossie: Generate the signed case dossier and close the case.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.section.statu: Badges show the current lifecycle status, severity, whether it is a recurrence, and whether the subject is redacted because they are off your team.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.section.overv: The overview card summarises the subject, sanction category, the linked exception, and the trigger and submission dates.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.section.dossi: Generate a downloadable HTML dossier with a SHA-256 integrity hash for the auditable disciplinary record.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.flow.trigger: An exception triggers a sanctions case
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.flow.recommen: A recommendation is drafted against the grid and submitted
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.flow.decision: HR records an outcome or the Disciplinary Committee decides
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.flow.appeal: The subject files an appeal and the authority decides it
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.flow.close: The case is closed and a dossier is generated
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.dep.exception: The linked exception that triggered this case
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.dep.grid: The sanctions grid supplying the recommended range and version
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.dep.directory: The user directory that resolves the unmasked subject name
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.use.dossier: The case dossier assembled for the disciplinary record
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.use.audit: The compliance audit trail of disciplinary actions
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.rule.lifecycl: Actions are gated by status — each step is only available in the correct lifecycle state.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.rule.deviatio: A recommendation outside the grid range requires a documented deviation reason.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.rule.masking: Subjects who are not on your team are masked as redacted throughout the case.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.rule.appeal: An appeal can be filed only after an HR outcome or a DC decision is recorded.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.tip.grid: Compare the recommendation to the grid range before submitting to keep decisions consistent.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.tip.dossier: Generate the dossier before closing so the exported record captures the final state.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.perm.recommen: Recommenders draft and submit sanction recommendations.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.perm.decide: HR and Disciplinary Committee members record outcomes and decisions.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.perm.view: Sanctions viewers can read the case and generate its dossier.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.faq.masked.q: Why is the subject shown as redacted?
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.faq.masked.a: The subject's identity is masked when they are not on your team, protecting privacy while you review the case.
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.faq.appeal.q: When can an appeal be filed?
sanctions.caseDetail.guide.faq.appeal.a: An appeal can be filed once an HR outcome or a Disciplinary Committee decision has been recorded, and the routed authority then decides it.
identity.userDetail.guide.purpose: Manage a single user's profile, role assignments, delegations, and account status.
identity.userDetail.guide.description: This page is the control panel for one user account. Review their profile and status, grant or revoke roles (globally or scoped to an org unit), and set up temporary delegations that let someone act on their behalf for a fixed period.
identity.userDetail.guide.action.grant: Grant a role to the user, optionally scoped to an org unit.
identity.userDetail.guide.action.revoke: Revoke an existing role assignment from the user.
identity.userDetail.guide.action.delegat: Create a time-boxed delegation of a role to another user.
identity.userDetail.guide.section.profil: Shows the user's name, email, account status, last login, and system ID for identification.
Lists the roles granted to the user with their scope; use Grant role to add one or the delete icon to revoke.
identity.userDetail.guide.section.delega: Temporary role delegations with a start and end date; create or revoke them to cover absences.
identity.userDetail.guide.flow.create: User account is created in the users list
identity.userDetail.guide.flow.grant: Roles are granted here, globally or per org unit
identity.userDetail.guide.flow.delegate: Delegations extend a role to a stand-in for a period
identity.userDetail.guide.flow.access: Effective permissions govern what the user can do across AuditX
identity.userDetail.guide.dep.users: User accounts managed in the identity module.
identity.userDetail.guide.dep.roles: Role definitions and their permission sets.
identity.userDetail.guide.dep.scopes: Org units that scope role assignments.
identity.userDetail.guide.use.audits: Audit assignments rely on the user's roles and permissions.
identity.userDetail.guide.use.approvals: Approval workflows resolve approvers from role assignments.
identity.userDetail.guide.use.audittrail: Every grant, revoke, and delegation is written to the audit trail.
identity.userDetail.guide.rule.scope: A role can be global or scoped to a single org unit; scope limits where its permissions apply.
identity.userDetail.guide.rule.delegatio: A delegation is active only between its start and end dates.
identity.userDetail.guide.rule.status: A deactivated account cannot sign in even if roles remain assigned.
identity.userDetail.guide.rule.selfServi: Users cannot grant or revoke their own roles; an administrator must do it.
identity.userDetail.guide.tip.scope: Scope roles to an org unit to grant least-privilege access instead of a global grant.
identity.userDetail.guide.tip.delegation: Use a delegation rather than a permanent role for planned leave or short-term cover.
identity.userDetail.guide.tip.review: Review the role list periodically and revoke assignments the user no longer needs.
identity.userDetail.guide.perm.admin: Identity administrators can grant and revoke roles and delegations.
identity.userDetail.guide.perm.manager: Managers can view the profile and manage delegations within their scope.
identity.userDetail.guide.faq.scope.q: What does a scoped role mean?
identity.userDetail.guide.faq.scope.a: A scoped role applies the role's permissions only within the selected org unit; a global role applies everywhere.
identity.userDetail.guide.faq.delegation: How is a delegation different from a role?
A delegation is a temporary grant that automatically expires on its end date, whereas a role assignment stays until revoked.
identity.roleEditor.guide.purpose: Define a role's permission set and inheritance so users get exactly the access they need.
identity.roleEditor.guide.description: This page creates or edits a role: its name, an optional inheritance from parent roles, and the permissions it grants from the catalogue, each constrained to a scope. Built-in system roles are shown read-only and cannot be changed.
identity.roleEditor.guide.action.details: Name the role and give it a clear description.
identity.roleEditor.guide.action.inherit: Inherit permissions from one or more parent roles.
identity.roleEditor.guide.action.permiss: Pick permissions from the catalogue and set each one's scope.
identity.roleEditor.guide.action.save: Save to create or update the role (subject to approval).
identity.roleEditor.guide.section.detail: Set the role name, description, and the parent roles it inherits permissions from.
identity.roleEditor.guide.section.permis: Expand each module to tick the permissions the role grants and choose the scope for each.
identity.roleEditor.guide.section.action: Commit your changes or discard them and return to the roles list.
identity.roleEditor.guide.flow.catalogue: Permission catalogue and existing roles are loaded
identity.roleEditor.guide.flow.define: Define the role's name, inheritance, and permissions
identity.roleEditor.guide.flow.approve: A second authoriser approves the change (maker-checker)
identity.roleEditor.guide.dep.catalogue: The permission catalogue that lists every grantable permission
identity.roleEditor.guide.dep.roles: Existing roles available as inheritance parents
identity.roleEditor.guide.dep.scopes: Scope levels (global, business unit, branch, self) that constrain each permission
identity.roleEditor.guide.use.users: Users are assigned this role to receive its access
identity.roleEditor.guide.use.access: Access control checks enforce the role's permissions across the app
identity.roleEditor.guide.use.audit: Role changes are recorded for the security audit trail
identity.roleEditor.guide.rule.builtIn: Built-in system roles are read-only and cannot be edited or deleted.
identity.roleEditor.guide.rule.permissio: A role must grant at least one permission before it can be saved.
identity.roleEditor.guide.rule.scope: A permission's scope can be narrowed only down to its finest allowed scope.
identity.roleEditor.guide.rule.makerChec: Saving may require a second authoriser's approval before it takes effect.
identity.roleEditor.guide.tip.inherit: Use inheritance to build layered roles instead of re-selecting shared permissions.
identity.roleEditor.guide.tip.leastPrivi: Grant the least privilege that still lets the role do its job.
identity.roleEditor.guide.tip.scope: Prefer the narrowest scope (branch or self) over global where possible.
identity.roleEditor.guide.perm.admin: Identity administrators can create and edit roles.
identity.roleEditor.guide.perm.viewer: Users without edit rights can view a role but not change it.
identity.roleEditor.guide.faq.builtIn.q: Why can't I edit this role?
identity.roleEditor.guide.faq.builtIn.a: It is a built-in system role, which is locked as read-only; create a custom role instead.
identity.roleEditor.guide.faq.inherit.q: What does inheriting from a parent role do?
identity.roleEditor.guide.faq.inherit.a: The role automatically gains all of its parent roles' permissions on top of the ones you select here.
engagement.board.guide.purpose: See every engagement you're part of and the one next step to take on each, at a glance.
engagement.board.guide.description: The Engagement Lifecycle board is your portfolio view across every audit you're on — its current stage, progress, and the role-scoped action the system has decided is next for you, with a button to act on it immediately.
engagement.board.guide.action.filter: Toggle 'Waiting on me' to see only engagements needing your action
engagement.board.guide.action.act: Click a card's action button to act on the next step directly
engagement.board.guide.action.journey: Open 'View journey' for the full stage-by-stage timeline
engagement.board.guide.section.toolbar.b: Filters the board down to engagements where the system has identified an action for you specifically.
engagement.board.guide.section.grid.body: Each card shows the audit's stage, progress and open-exception count, with its next best action as a button — no need to hunt through the audit to find what to do next.
engagement.board.guide.rule.nextAction: The next action shown is scoped to your role on the engagement — auditors, leads and auditees each see a different action at the same stage.
engagement.board.guide.rule.roleGated: You only see engagements where you're a team member or otherwise have visibility.
engagement.board.guide.tip.waiting: Use 'Waiting on me' at the start of your day to triage what needs attention first.
engagement.board.guide.tip.progress: The progress bar tracks checklist responses — 100% doesn't necessarily mean the audit is closed, just fieldwork-complete.
engagement.board.guide.faq.action.q: How does the system decide my next action?
engagement.board.guide.faq.action.a: It reads the audit's current lifecycle stage plus your role on the team and, for remediation, exception ownership — then resolves the single next step that makes sense for you.
engagement.journey.guide.purpose: Follow one engagement's lifecycle stage by stage, with the current step's action front and centre.
engagement.journey.guide.description: A vertical timeline of every stage an engagement passes through, from setup to closure. Completed stages are marked done, the current stage is highlighted with your next action, and future stages are greyed out until their turn.
engagement.journey.guide.action.act: Act on the highlighted next-step button at the current stage
engagement.journey.guide.section.timelin: Each stage shows as done, current or pending. Only the current stage can be acted on from here.
engagement.journey.guide.section.next.bo: The action(s) available to you right now, scoped to your role. A route action opens the screen that performs the step; a transition action advances the audit inline.
engagement.journey.guide.rule.currentOnl: Only the current stage offers an action; past and future stages are read-only history.
engagement.journey.guide.rule.roleGated: The action shown depends on your role — a lead may see a transition, while a team member sees a route into the performing screen.
engagement.journey.guide.tip.exceptions: The open-exceptions count in the header flags remediation work still outstanding, even if fieldwork is complete.
engagement.journey.guide.faq.noAction.q: Why does the current stage show no action for me?
engagement.journey.guide.faq.noAction.a: The next best action is role-scoped — if nothing is waiting specifically on your role at this stage, the timeline says so rather than showing an action that isn't yours to take.
ac.plansAwaiting.guide.purpose: Give the AC chair a single queue of annual plans that need a decision.
ac.plansAwaiting.guide.description: Every submitted or revision-submitted annual plan lands here for review. Expand a plan to see its item count, add a discussion comment, or open it to approve, reject or request a revision.
ac.plansAwaiting.guide.action.expand: Expand a plan to see its period and item count
ac.plansAwaiting.guide.action.comment: Add an AC discussion comment on a plan
ac.plansAwaiting.guide.action.decide: Open the plan to review and decide
ac.plansAwaiting.guide.section.list.body: Grouped by plan period, newest submissions included. Each entry shows its submission status and period dates.
ac.plansAwaiting.guide.rule.chairOnly: Only the Audit Committee Chair may record the approve/reject/revision decision.
ac.plansAwaiting.guide.rule.revision: A revision request returns the plan to the planning team for changes and resubmission.
ac.plansAwaiting.guide.tip.comments: Use the comment box to leave context for the chair's decision before it's recorded.
ac.plansAwaiting.guide.faq.decide.q: Where do I actually approve or reject a plan?
