ac.plansAwaiting.guide.faq.decide.a: This screen is a queue — open the plan ("Review & decide") to record the decision on the existing plan-detail screen.
ac.restrictVisibility.title: Restrict finding visibility
ac.restrictVisibility.subtitle: Limit who may see this finding's detail. Others see a restricted placeholder.
ac.restrictVisibility.guide.purpose: Let a Chief Internal Auditor limit a sensitive finding's detail to a named allow-list.
ac.restrictVisibility.guide.description: Some findings are sensitive enough that only specific people should see the full detail. Set an allow-list here; everyone else sees a restricted placeholder instead of the finding's content.
ac.restrictVisibility.guide.action.selec: Choose the users allowed to see the finding's detail
ac.restrictVisibility.guide.action.apply: Apply the restriction, optionally with a reason
ac.restrictVisibility.guide.section.form: Leave it empty to fall back to the default chair/CIA audience; select specific users to hand-pick who may view the finding.
ac.restrictVisibility.guide.rule.default: An empty allow-list restricts visibility to the default chair/CIA audience, not to everyone.
ac.restrictVisibility.guide.rule.filtere: The backend filters at read time per requester — there is no separate 'restricted' copy of the finding.
ac.restrictVisibility.guide.tip.reason: Recording a reason helps a later reviewer understand why the restriction was applied.
templatesAdmin.editor.guide.purpose: Build and maintain a checklist template's structure through its draft → published lifecycle.
templatesAdmin.editor.guide.description: Set the template's name, audit type and description, then build its checklist as sections of ordered items. Once published, a template is locked — editing again creates a new draft version.
templatesAdmin.editor.guide.action.items: Add or edit checklist items within a section
templatesAdmin.editor.guide.action.reord: Drag to reorder sections and items
templatesAdmin.editor.guide.action.publi: Publish a draft, or start a new draft from a published version
templatesAdmin.editor.guide.section.deta: The name, audit type and description. The audit type is fixed once the template exists — it decides which audits can use it.
templatesAdmin.editor.guide.section.stru: Drag sections and items to reorder them, including moving an item across sections. Only editable while the template is a draft.
templatesAdmin.editor.guide.section.life: Publish a finished draft so audits can start using it, or start a new draft from a published template to make further changes.
templatesAdmin.editor.guide.use.audits: New audits copy a published template's checklist
templatesAdmin.editor.guide.rule.draftOn: Sections and items are only editable while the template is a draft.
templatesAdmin.editor.guide.rule.immutab: The audit type cannot change once the template exists — create a new template instead.
templatesAdmin.editor.guide.rule.newDraf: Editing a published template creates a new draft version; the published version audits already used stays unchanged.
templatesAdmin.editor.guide.tip.dragDrop: Drag the handle icon to reorder — items can be dropped into a different section.
templatesAdmin.editor.guide.faq.editPubl: Can I edit a published template directly?
No — publishing locks it. Use 'New draft version' to start an editable copy; audits already using the published version are unaffected.
account.prefs.guide.purpose: Choose how AuditX reaches you for non-critical notifications.
account.prefs.guide.description: Critical notifications always reach you. These two toggles control lower-priority channels: SMS for non-critical alerts, and batching routine notifications into a digest instead of one-by-one.
account.prefs.guide.action.sms: Toggle SMS delivery for non-critical alerts
account.prefs.guide.action.digests: Toggle batching routine notifications into a digest
account.prefs.guide.section.toggles.body: Changes save immediately and apply to future notifications only.
account.prefs.guide.rule.criticalAlways: Critical notifications (e.g. security and compliance alerts) are never suppressed by these preferences.
universe.dims.guide.purpose: Define the weighted dimensions used to score every auditable entity's inherent and residual risk.
universe.dims.guide.description: Each dimension (e.g. financial impact, regulatory exposure) has a weight and a rating scale. Together they produce the composite risk score that drives audit-universe prioritisation and the risk heatmap.
universe.dims.guide.action.edit: Edit a dimension's weight or scale
universe.dims.guide.action.filter: Filter to active, inactive, or all dimensions
universe.dims.guide.section.table.title: The dimension list
universe.dims.guide.section.table.body: Each dimension's weight and rating scale (min–max). Deactivating a dimension stops it being scored on new assessments without deleting its history.
universe.dims.guide.rule.weight: A dimension's weight determines how much it contributes to an entity's composite risk score.
universe.dims.guide.rule.scale: Every score entered against a dimension must fall within its configured min–max scale.
universe.dims.guide.rule.deactivate: Deactivating a dimension preserves historic scores but excludes it from new assessments.
universe.dims.guide.tip.weights: Keep weights proportionate across dimensions — a single overweighted dimension can dominate the composite score.
orgUnit.list.guide.purpose: Maintain the department/business-unit hierarchy that entities, users and scorecards roll up to.
orgUnit.list.guide.description: A tree of organisational units, from Head Office down. Auditable entities and users are each assigned to a unit, and department scorecards aggregate audit and exception data by this hierarchy.
orgUnit.list.guide.action.create: Create a new org unit under a parent
orgUnit.list.guide.action.reparent: Rename a unit or move it under a different parent
orgUnit.list.guide.action.archive: Archive a unit no longer in use, or restore one
orgUnit.list.guide.section.tree.title: The org-unit tree
orgUnit.list.guide.section.tree.body: Indented by depth from Head Office. Archived units are hidden by default — tick 'Include archived' to see them.
orgUnit.list.guide.rule.noCycles: Re-parenting is rejected if it would create a cycle in the hierarchy.
orgUnit.list.guide.rule.uniqueCode: Each unit's code must be unique across the hierarchy.
orgUnit.list.guide.rule.archiveKeepsHist: Archiving a unit hides it from new assignments but keeps its historic data intact.
orgUnit.list.guide.tip.indent: Indentation shows depth — use it to spot a unit's place in the hierarchy at a glance.
audits.exec.guide.purpose: Do the fieldwork: respond to checklist items, attach evidence and raise findings, all from one screen.
audits.exec.guide.description: The dedicated execution screen for an audit's checklist. Respond to each item, attach supporting evidence, log time, and raise an exception directly where a control fails — without leaving the checklist.
audits.exec.guide.action.respond: Record a response and verdict against a checklist item
audits.exec.guide.action.evidence: Attach evidence files to an item
audits.exec.guide.action.exception: Raise an exception directly from a failed item
audits.exec.guide.action.time: Log time spent against the audit
audits.exec.guide.use.exceptions: Exceptions raised here feed the exception register
audits.exec.guide.use.reports: Completed responses feed the generated report
audits.exec.guide.rule.autoReview: Once every checklist item has a response, the audit automatically advances to Under Review.
audits.exec.guide.rule.assignment: An item can carry an assignment rule scoping who may respond to it.
audits.exec.guide.tip.evidence: Attach evidence at the item level so a reviewer can trace each response back to its support.
reports.panel.guide.purpose: Generate, track and download this audit's standalone report versions.
reports.panel.guide.description: Every report ever generated for this audit, each version sealed with a SHA-256 hash at completion. Generate a new version once the audit is under review or completed; download any completed version in its produced formats.
reports.panel.guide.action.generate: Generate a new report version (optionally with a DOCX export)
reports.panel.guide.action.download: Download a completed version in an available format
reports.panel.guide.action.open: Open a version to view, distribute or verify its hash
reports.panel.guide.section.generate.bod: Only enabled once the audit reaches Under Review or Completed — generating earlier would report on an incomplete fieldwork.
reports.panel.guide.section.table.title: Report versions
reports.panel.guide.section.table.body: Every generated version with its status, request time and sealed hash. A running generation polls automatically until it settles.
reports.panel.guide.dep.status: Audit must be Under Review or Completed
reports.panel.guide.use.ac: Audit Committee packs can include generated reports
reports.panel.guide.rule.states: A report moves through pending → running → completed (or failed); only completed reports can be downloaded or distributed.
reports.panel.guide.rule.hash: Every completed report is sealed with a SHA-256 hash at generation time, verifiable later from the report viewer.
reports.panel.guide.tip.docx: Tick 'Also generate DOCX' before generating if you need an editable copy alongside the standard export.
reports.panel.guide.faq.disabled.q: Why is the Generate button disabled?
reports.panel.guide.faq.disabled.a: Report generation is only available once the audit has reached Under Review or Completed, so the report reflects finished fieldwork.
reports.viewer.guide.purpose: View, verify, distribute and share one report version.
reports.viewer.guide.description: The single source of truth for a completed report: an inline preview of the exact sealed content, hash verification against tampering, distribution to recipients, and the distribution log.
reports.viewer.guide.action.preview: Preview the sealed HTML content before exporting
reports.viewer.guide.action.verify: Verify the report's hash hasn't changed since generation
reports.viewer.guide.action.distribute: Distribute the report to named recipients
reports.viewer.guide.section.overview.bo: Version, status, sealed hash and generation timestamps at a glance.
reports.viewer.guide.section.distributio: Every recipient this version was sent to, with its delivery outcome — confirm pending deliveries as delivered or bounced.
reports.viewer.guide.dep.panel: Generated from the audit's reports panel
reports.viewer.guide.use.ac: Audit Committee packs reference distributed reports
reports.viewer.guide.use.sharedLinks: Shareable links resolve back to this viewer
reports.viewer.guide.rule.sealed: A completed report's content is immutable — its hash is sealed at generation and never recomputed from live data.
reports.viewer.guide.rule.pending: Preview, download, verify and distribute are only available once the report has completed.
reports.viewer.guide.tip.verify: Run 'Verify hash' before relying on a downloaded copy to confirm it matches what was sealed at generation.
reports.viewer.guide.faq.hash.q: What does the SHA-256 hash actually protect against?
reports.viewer.guide.faq.hash.a: It proves the downloaded file is byte-for-byte what was generated and sealed — 'Verify hash' recomputes it and flags any mismatch, e.g. from tampering or corruption.
analytics.view.guide.purpose: See a live dashboard's widgets, each backed by a real-time analytics query.
analytics.view.guide.description: A dashboard is a named collection of widgets — key figures, tables and charts — each computed from the current data. Widgets you don't have permission for degrade to a locked placeholder rather than being hidden outright.
analytics.view.guide.action.addWidget: Add a widget to this dashboard
analytics.view.guide.action.removeWidget: Remove a widget from this dashboard
analytics.view.guide.action.refresh: Refresh all widgets with the latest data
analytics.view.guide.section.widgets.bod: Each widget renders as a key-figure grid, chart or table depending on its data shape. GUID columns in tables resolve to names automatically.
analytics.view.guide.rule.gated: A widget you lack permission for shows a locked placeholder instead of its data — it is never silently hidden.
analytics.view.guide.rule.live: Widget data is computed live on each load, not cached from when the widget was added.
analytics.view.guide.tip.drilldown: Table widgets often link onward — e.g. into the exception or audit the row represents.
analytics.view.guide.faq.unavailable.q: Why does a widget say data is unavailable?
analytics.view.guide.faq.unavailable.a: The backend degrades a widget you don't have permission to view to a locked placeholder rather than an error, so the rest of the dashboard still renders normally.
analytics.detail.guide.purpose: Drill into one recurrence cluster and its member findings.
analytics.detail.guide.description: A recurrence cluster groups closed findings that recur against the same entity/category within a detection window — a signal that a control isn't holding. This screen shows the cluster's facts and every member finding.
analytics.detail.guide.action.open: Open a member finding's full exception detail
analytics.detail.guide.section.summary.b: The detection window, first/last occurrence, and when the cluster was detected and notified.

templatesAdmin.ratingScales.title: Rating Scales
templatesAdmin.ratingScales.subtitle: Reusable labelled scales for Rating-type checklist items, and the score each point earns.

templatesAdmin.ratingScales.guide.descri: A rating scale is a set of points (e.g. 1=Poor .. 5=Excellent), each carrying a 0-100 score. Any checklist item using the Rating response type references one scale; the auditor's chosen point drives post-response scoring.

templatesAdmin.ratingScales.guide.rule.s: The score an auditor's response earns comes directly from the point they select on the item's configured scale.
templatesAdmin.ratingScales.guide.rule.d: Deactivating a scale preserves it for items that already reference it but hides it from new item configuration.
templatesAdmin.ratingScales.guide.tip.re: Reuse one scale across many templates rather than creating near-duplicates — it keeps scoring consistent.
exceptionRules.title: Exception-raising rules
exceptionRules.subtitle: Configure which finalised responses, beyond a Fail, can have an exception raised against them.
exceptionRules.error.load: We couldn't load the exception-raising rules.
exceptionRules.emptyMessage: By default an exception can only be raised on a Fail. Add a rule to extend that to N/A or a low score for a response type.
exceptionRules.field.scoreThresholdHint: A response scoring at or below this (0-100) becomes eligible. Leave blank to disable score-gating.
exceptionRules.guide.purpose: Configure which finalised responses, beyond a Fail verdict, are eligible to have an exception raised against them.
exceptionRules.guide.description: A Fail verdict is always exception-eligible and needs no rule. Each rule extends eligibility for one response type: allow raising on an N/A verdict, and/or on a response scoring at or below a threshold (e.g. a poor Rating). Response types with no rule keep the default Fail-only behaviour.
exceptionRules.guide.action.create: Add a rule for a response type
exceptionRules.guide.action.edit: Edit a rule's conditions or deactivate it
exceptionRules.guide.section.table.title: The rule list
exceptionRules.guide.section.table.body: One row per response type that has an extended rule, showing whether N/A is allowed and any score threshold. Deactivating a rule reverts that response type to Fail-only.
exceptionRules.guide.rule.failAlways: A Fail verdict is always exception-eligible — no rule can remove that.
exceptionRules.guide.rule.onePerType: At most one rule per response type.
exceptionRules.guide.tip.score: Score-gating only affects Rating items, which are the only response type that earns a score.

rootCauseGaps.guide.purpose: Track systemic root-cause weaknesses that recur across findings, from identification to closure.
rootCauseGaps.guide.description: When the same underlying cause drives several findings, remediating each in isolation misses the pattern. A root-cause gap groups the contributing findings under one owner with a target date and an open→closed lifecycle, so the systemic fix is tracked and evidenced.

rootCauseGaps.guide.rule.lock: A closed gap is locked; reopen it to change its details or links.
rootCauseGaps.guide.tip.recurring: The exceptions tracker flags recurring findings — those are prime candidates to group under a gap.
